top_10.title: RSpamD documentation is missing
top_10.body:
Documentation is missing for Rspamd when installing Modoboa manually/without installer. Installation and configuration instructions would be helpful.

Besides the content of the various configuration files these settings are needed:
```
arc.conf
  selector_map = "%selector_map_path";
  path_map = "%key_map_path";

dkim_signing.conf
  selector_map = "%selector_map_path"
  path_map = "%key_map_path";

dmarc.conf
  email = 'postmaster@%hostname'; # Source of DMARC reports
  domain = '%hostname'; # Domain to serve
  org_name = '%hostname'; # Organisation

groups.conf
  weight = %whitelist_auth_weigth;

settings.conf
  %{whitelist_auth_enabled}  symbols ["WHITELIST_AUTHENTICATED"];

worker-controller.inc
  enable_password = %controller_password`
```

CUDA and HIP input import a `static __constant__` local without an initializer as an uninitialized Metal local, so the kernel reads indeterminate values
OpenCL input binds a program-scope `__constant` array at the binding of the kernel's first buffer, so Metal output refuses it
The agent skill's first command, uvx datamodel-codegen --help, fails because no package of that name exists
top_10.body:
When running `uvx datamodel-codegen --help`, it raises error because the package name on PyPI is `datamodel-code-generator`.

Steps to reproduce:
```bash
uvx datamodel-codegen --help
```

top_10.title: Flaky: test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt (fixed 60 ms sleep before reading flushed frame)
top_10.body:
`test/test_subagent_scale_batch.py::TestCoalescer::test_tool_merge_clears_stale_retrying_attempt` failed on an unrelated PR.

- Run: https://github.com/kirodotdev/KiroCrew/actions/runs/41797479802/job/126467561880 (PR #29490, head 712e6f822c65)
- OS: ubuntu, Python 3.12, Backend Tests shard 3
- Failing line: `((etype, data),) = all_frames` -> `ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 1, got 0)`

The test waits a fixed `await asyncio.sleep(0.06)` past the 20 ms flush tick and then expects one frame. On a slow runner the flush has not happened yet, so the list is empty. It passes 8/8 locally (alone and with the whole file under -n 4). PR #29490 does not touch the coalescer or this test.

Likely fix: wait for the frame (poll with a deadline) instead of a fixed sleep.

top_10.title: Church name text hidden in sidebar but still shown on login page when a custom logo is uploaded
top_10.body:
## Description When a custom church logo is uploaded (Admin → System → Church Information), the church-name text is hidden in the sidebar but still shown on the login page — inconsistent behavior across the two surfaces that both render the logo. - **Sidebar** (`src/Include/Header.php`, lines ~186-199): the `navbar-brand-text` span is wrapped in `if (ChurchLogoService::hasCustomLogo())` — it only renders when there's **no** custom logo: ```php 'navbar-brand-image crm-brand-logo']) ?> ... ``` - **Login page** (`src/session/templates/begin-session.php`, lines 30-37): `ChurchLogo::img()` and `ChurchMetaData::getChurchName()` render unconditionally as separate elements, with no `hasCustomLogo()` check at all: ```php

``` Confirmed identical on both `master` and the `7.8.1` tag (same blob SHA on `begin-session.php` across both refs). The sidebar's hide-on-custom-logo behavior was intentional per #9719 ("The uploaded logo replaces the ChurchCRM branding in the sidebar (where it also hides the church-name text)") on the assumption that an uploaded logo already contains the church name as artwork. The login page not following the same rule means that assumption isn't applied consistently — admins who want the name visible lose it in the sidebar but keep it on login, with no way to choose. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Admin → System → Church Information → upload a custom logo. 2. Visit the dashboard — sidebar shows only the logo, no church name. 3. Log out and view the login page — logo **and** church name are both shown. ## Expected Consistent behavior between the sidebar and the login page — either both hide the name when a custom logo is present, or neither does. ## Reported by maestrovivo, in the project's Discord #support-chat.

Docs: stale statements about the chat screen, dictation and image intake found in the chat-ui test campaign
top_10.body:
The chat-ui test campaign (PR #741) found these while checking what the docs say against the code. Line numbers are at the campaign's merge base.

- [ ] **rag-design.md ~:666** names a `scopeChipLabel` helper that does not exist; the "Answering from" label is computed inline in `ScopePopover.tsx` (~:240-280).
- [x] **rag-design.md §15.5 / §15.7 (~:2458-2464, ~:2539)** still describe the pre-D69 meter: a "Context: 6.4k / 8k" tooltip and a progressbar with `aria-valuetext`. Today it is a `role="meter"` labelled "Memory" with a "… % full (about 6.4k of 8k tokens)" tooltip (`ContextMeter.tsx`). (PR #776: both now describe the `role="meter"` "Memory" meter and its bands)
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:2377** (Voice dictation) says the "not installed" mic deep-links with `onNavigate('models')`; since #527 it is `models:voice` (`ChatScreen.tsx` ~:2681).
- [ ] **architecture.md ~:12739** (Image understanding §5) says decode "re-encodes to the input MIME"; since #124 a WEBP becomes PNG (`decode.ts` `outputMimeFor`, ~:111; §11 already says so).
- [ ] **Code comments:** `renderer/lib/displayMap.ts` ~:146-148 repeats the "lands on an odd index" claim that #741 corrected in AssistantMarkdown (with one capture group the split always ends on prose), and `shared/citation-markers.ts` ~:18 and displayMap say `normalizeMathDelimiters` lives in Transcript.tsx (it is in AssistantMarkdown.tsx).
- [x] **ChatScreen.tsx ~:1834-1836**: the stream `finally` comment promises the "Stopped" toast only when no error explained the early end; the condition never reads the error (see #742). (PR #776: the condition now reads `sendSucceeded`, and the comment says why)

issues.title: [Request] 文档：Secure Boot 开启下的自签流程（db 自签 / MOK+shim）与三个已知坑
issues.body:
> 起草说明：本文由 AI 辅助整理，事实来自仓库现状与 #145 的讨论；**没有做真机验证**（我这台没有可切 Secure Boot 的独显机位），凡未实测之处都已标注。若与现场不符，以现场为准。

### 建议类型 / Request type

文档修正 / Documentation change

### 当前问题与需求 / Current problem and need

**要解决的是文档缺口，不是功能缺口。** 想让 Secure Boot 保持开启的用户，现在在文档里只能读到一句：

- `docs/faq.md:272` / `docs/faq.en.md:263`：`替换 U 盘启动文件前先备份。Secure Boot 关闭或使用受信任的自签 EFI。`

这句话承认了自签这条路存在，但没有过程。而 [#145](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/145)（已关闭）里三条路只写全了一条：

| #145 里的方案 | 文档状态 |
|---|---|
| 方案一 休眠切换法（SB 开/关来回切） | 评论里有完整流程，未入 FAQ |
| 方案二 固件内置 FFS（PR #100） | `docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162` 有可行性，标注【待实证】 |
| 方案三 MOK + shim | 评论里有六步，未入 FAQ |
| 方案三 db 自签 | **只有"简版"一句**：每台机器手动导证书、每次更新重签 |

而现场反馈指向的恰恰是最后这条：#145 里有一条西语报告——"Conseguí firmar con un certificado propio el Efi, de modo que ha sido posible iniciar con el secure boot activado"（用自己的证书签了 EFI，因此可以在 Secure Boot 开启下启动）。这是 db 自签路线**可用**的现场证据，但它现在埋在一条已关闭的 issue 的评论区里，既没进 FAQ，也没进兼容性记录。

现实需求面也不小：#145 的原始动机是打 LoL/Vanguard（反作弊要求 SB 开启），而 `docs/community-reports.md` 里的实测行几乎每条都写着 "Secure Boot off"——SB-on 场景目前是文档空白区。

补充一点定位：这**不是**在申请"绕过 Secure Boot"。自签属 `SECURITY.md:53` 威胁模型里"已开启 Secure Boot 且已导入自签证书"的合法配置，与方案一、方案二并列，只是缺文档。

### 期望改进 / Desired improvement

新增 `docs/faq.md#secureboot`（EN 同步 `docs/faq.en.md`）一节，建议内容：

1. **两条路线对比表**：db 自签（固件直接验你的签名，代价是每台导证 + 每次重签）vs MOK+shim（不动 db，走发行版 shim）。shim 那条直接链接 #145 现有六步，不重复写。
2. **db 自签五步**：
   - 生成密钥/证书（`openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -addext "extendedKeyUsage=codeSigning"`——这个 EKU 不能省，Windows 侧 `signtool` 会校验）；
   - 签名与验证（`sbsign --key ... --cert ... --output ...`；`sbverify --cert ...`；Windows 等价物 `signtool sign /fd SHA256` + `signtool verify /pa`）；
   - 把 **DER 证书追加**进 db 的三种方式：固件 Key Management（`db → Append / Append from file`）、`efitools` 的 `efi-updatevar -a -c cert.crt -k KEK.key db`、`sbctl enroll-keys --microsoft`（`--microsoft` 才会把微软证书一并写回）；
   - 新版 maker 直接吃签名后的件：`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284`（`-BootEfi`）、`:488`（盘根）、`:494`（`EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`），即
     ```powershell
     .\make-usbroot.ps1 -Family ad102 -Out G:\ -BootEfi .\BOOTX64.signed.efi
     ```
   - 验证：`mokutil --sb-state` 应为 `SecureBoot enabled`；固件层真正放行的铁证是盘上出现新的 `loader.log` 且含 `TX BUILD` banner。
3. **三条硬纪律**（这部分比签名本身更容易出事）：
   - **只能追加，不能替换 db 里的微软证书**——`bootmgfw.efi` 靠 *Microsoft Windows Production PCA 2011* 签名，删了 Windows 起不来；
   - **动 PK 前先导出 PK/KEK/db 备份**；若板子要求清 PK 进 Setup Mode 才能 Append，事后必须把原厂证书恢复并重新 enroll PK；
   - **私钥只留本机**：db 里一旦有你的证书，这把私钥就能给这台机器签任何引导组件。
4. **三个已知坑**：
   - **SB 开着时 `ssdiag` 仍然不可用**：它临时加载的 `pmxdrv.sys` 是 Intel/COMODO 2018 交叉签名、无微软根，SB-ON 必然被 DSE 拒（`tools/ssdiag/README.md` 的 "Secure Boot — the gate that actually refuses this driver"、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`）。所以 SB 常开的机器上，系统内读回只能走 `loader.log` 的 `HANDOFF-OUT`（EFI 阶段零驱动读回）或 Linux 侧 `tools/diag-unlock.py`；要 `ssdiag --reapply` 修回锁，仍须临时关一次 SB。
   - **BitLocker / PCR[7]**：SB 或 db 状态变化会改 PCR[7]，可能弹恢复密钥，操作前先挂起保护。
   - **换版本必须重签**，签名后再改一个字节即失效；资产 `*.bin` 不需要签名（SB 只验 PE 引导链）。
5. **反作弊边界**（与 #145 的警告保持一致）：db 自签不改 SB 状态位，Vanguard（LoL）通常可过；ACE 系（腾讯）会校验 TPM/PCR[7] 链式启动记录，自签链的度量与原厂引导不同，**不保证过检**——打 ACE 系游戏请回到方案一。

顺带把 `docs/faq.md:272` / `.en.md:263` 那句改成带锚点的链接。

### 相关版本、文档与参考资料 / Versions, documentation and references

- 文档现状：`docs/faq.md:272`、`docs/faq.en.md:263`（自签仅一句）
- 讨论：#145（休眠切换法、FFS 方案、MOK+shim 六步、db 自签简版）；西语现场反馈在该 issue 评论中
- 固件形态可行性：`docs/dxe-driver-ffs-feasibility.md:162`（SB 只验 OS 引导链）
- maker 的 boot 路径改动：`5684752`（打印可执行 copy 步骤）、`c0f3518`（输出不再纯平铺）、`release/make-usbroot.ps1:284/488/494/500/505-511`
- ssdiag 的 SB 门：`tools/ssdiag/README.md`、`docs/ssdiag-platform-gates.md`
- 威胁模型定位：`SECURITY.md:53`
- FAQ 判据/回锁值（本 issue 不涉及，仅说明读回路径不同）：`docs/faq.md:189`、`docs/cold-values.md:139`

### 替代方案与补充信息 / Alternatives and additional context

- **替代**：维持现状，让每个 SB-on 用户自己在 Discussions 问一遍。现状的代价是 #145 已经被关掉，新来的人搜不到过程。
- **更小的一步**：只把这份内容作为 #145 的补充评论贴回去——但该单已关闭，不解决"下次还能找到吗"。
- **我愿意直接出 patch**：如果维护者认可，可以照 #141 / #144 的方式提 docs PR，中英同步、只动 `docs/faq*.md`。
- **缺一个现场字段**：能否请 #145 那位西语报告者补 **主板型号** 与 **`ssdiag` 是否被拒**（第 4 条里"必然被拒"还是"通常被拒"取决于此），以及 **BitLocker 是否弹过恢复密钥**。这三项决定文档该写成硬性结论还是保守表述。

issues.title: [Report] RTX 4060 Laptop (28A0) / MECHREVO Yaoshi15Pro 2024 (GM5IX0A, i7-14650HX) - v2.1.9 TX success, matched A/B FP16 +81%, 15-inch thin laptop @ 140 W
issues.body:
## 摘要 / Summary

`10de:28a0`（AD107 · 24 SM · 8 GB）在机械革命 **耀世15Pro 2024**（i7-14650HX / 32 GB）上完成 **v2.1.9 Ada 事务**，EFI 侧读回全绿（`HANDOFF-OUT: ss0=0x88888888 ss1=0x8 readout1=0x00000000 feat_plm=0xffffffff`），Windows 正常进入。

**平台定位需要先说明**：这是一台 **15 寸轻薄游戏本**，不是同 TGP 的厚砖机。140 W 塞进这个厚度的机身，散热余量本来就是这个形态的短板——下面的 87 ℃ / 2.5 GHz 持续数据要放在这个前提下看，不代表其他 140 W 机型的水平。

同一脚本、同一 GPU 设置（140 W / 核心 +105 MHz / 显存 +200 MHz）的前后对照：

| 路径 | 解锁前 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.26 / 21.27 | **38.45** | **+81%** |
| BF16 | 21.25 / 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 / 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3 | 40.79 / 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（对照） | 6.41 / 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

绝对值比 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）和 [#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882）低 13–15%，实测受 **140 W 功耗墙 + 87 ℃ 温度墙**限制（持续负载下核心 2625 → 2430 MHz），与这台 15 寸轻薄机身的散热包络相符。新增信息：28a0 的首份**同脚本匹配 A/B**，以及解锁态下的持续功耗/时钟/温度采样。

---

## 工具版本 / Tool version

- **nv-uefi-unlocker v2.1.9** 官方发布包，未做任何本地修改
- `BOOTX64.EFI` 335,872 B，SHA-256 `9D2C41F90B290AD0DA3ECF294016A7EA67638E2625D8E1B1735028298943BB5C`（与 [#35](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/35) 记录的官方 v2.1.9 同一文件）
- 资产：`-Family 40` 生成的 `ad102` family 共 8 个文件，`loader.log` 中逐个 `TX-ASSET-DIAG: ... loaded N/N bytes` 全量校验通过
- 未使用 `i_know_what_i_am_doing.txt` / `tx-quiet.txt` / `tx-select-bdf.txt` / `tx-require-d0.txt` 等任何 marker（日志中均为 `absent`）

## GPU 与平台 / GPU and platform

## 性能对比 / Performance comparison

**口径**：`make-usbroot.ps1` 自带前的自写脚本 `gemm_bench.py`（`torch.mm`，8192 系尺寸扫，`cudaEvent` 计时，每尺寸 5 次预热 + 3 窗口 × 20 次取中位），**解锁前后同脚本、同 GPU 设置**；解锁前为上一次启动（stock），解锁后为事务后同一次启动，两次测量间隔约 40 分钟，期间未改任何 GPU 设置。

**A/B（N=4096，TF/s）**

| 路径 | stock 第1次 | stock 第2次 | 解锁后 | 变化 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP16 | 21.27 | 21.26 | **38.45** | +81% |
| BF16 | 21.25 | 21.48 | 38.66 | +80% |
| TF32 | 10.25 | 10.80 | 18.57 | +79% |
| FP8 e4m3（`_scaled_mm`） | 40.79 | 41.32 | 74.88 | +85% |
| FP32（TF32 off，对照） | 6.41 | 6.94 | 6.52 | 持平 |
| 显存 copy（对照） | 153.8 GB/s | 153.0 GB/s | 150.0 GB/s | 持平 |

`FP16 / FP8` 比值：stock 0.52 → 解锁后 0.51；`FP16 / FP32` 比值：stock 3.1× → 解锁后 5.9×。三条对照（FP32、显存带宽、以及时钟本身）都持平，说明增益不是时钟或散热瞬态造成的。

**其他尺寸（解锁后，同一脚本）**：FP16 1024 → 42.51，4096 → 38.45，8192 → 35.46。

**第二套独立基准交叉验证**：用 [#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119) 附件里的 `baseline-gemm-v1.py` 原样跑（N=4096、`torch.mm(a,b,out=c)`、7 组 × 30 次、每组一个 event 窗口）：**FP16 37.587 TF/s，BF16 38.227 TF/s**，与本机自写脚本的 38.45 / 38.66 一致（差 2%）。

**持续负载（解锁后，FP16 GEMM 4096，连续 40 s）**

| 指标 | 值 |
|---|---|
| 吞吐 | 36.06 TF/s（40 s 平均） |
| 核心时钟 | 2625 → 2430 MHz，均值 **2545 MHz** |
| 功耗 | 均值 132 W，峰值 **139.8 W**（顶死 140 W TGP） |
| 温度 | 79 → **87 ℃**（控制台 `TargetTemperature` 即为 87） |

**与现有报告的对比（仅供维护者参考，不作结论）**：[#119](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/119)（28e0）stock 29.51 → 44.24；[#124](https://github.com/physicsdolphin/nv-uefi-unlocker/issues/124)（2882 桌面）n=4096 FP16 26.98 → 42.44。本机 stock 21.26 明显更低但增益更大（+81% vs +49% / +57%）。解锁后绝对值低 13–15%，而 **每 MHz 效率与 #119 接近**（本机 36.06 / 2545 MHz ≈ 14.2 GFLOPS/MHz；按其 44.24 反推约 3.0 GHz 得 ~14.7），因此**我倾向于认为这是 140 W 笔记本散热包络下的频率差异，而非解锁不完整**——这一条是假设，没有 ssdiag 读回佐证。

issues.title: First time contributing? Start here.
issues.body:
Welcome 👋

If you've never contributed to AiSOC before, here's the shortest path from "interesting repo" to "merged PR".

## Step 1 — See AiSOC actually running

```bash
git clone https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC && cd AiSOC
make up      # the CORE profile — the real pipeline
make smoke   # prove it: one real event in, a retrievable alert out
```

`make up` creates `.env`, generates every secret in it, creates an administrator and **prints its password once** — copy it. Then sign in at <http://localhost:3000> (API docs at <http://localhost:8000/api/docs>). `make smoke` reports PASS or FAIL for each stage, so you know the pipeline works rather than assuming it:

```
[PASS] raw telemetry accepted by ingest
[PASS] event traversed the spine and became an alert
[PASS] alert is retrievable by id from the API
```

Needs Docker Compose v2 with 8 GB memory and 20 GB free disk in the Docker VM, plus `python3` and `bash`. `make doctor` checks all of it and diagnoses a stack that won't come up. [Installation](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/installation) says what each number was measured against.

**Zero install:** [open in GitHub Codespaces](https://codespaces.new/beenuar/AiSOC?quickstart=1) and run the same commands, then click the forwarded port 3000 in the **Ports** panel.

Once it's up, `make demo` loads labelled synthetic data on top — including `/cases/INC-RT-001?tab=ledger`, a LockBit 3.0 ransomware case the agent has investigated. Click through the **Investigation Ledger** so you've seen what AiSOC does. Every seeded row carries `is_synthetic=true` and the console labels it as such.

> One thing to avoid: `pnpm aisoc:demo` brings up `infra/compose/docker-compose.demo.yml`, which is a **UI preview only** — no ingest service, no fusion service, and Kafka disabled. The file says so in its own header. It's fine for looking at the interface, but it can't tell you whether AiSOC works. Use `make up` for that.

## Step 2 — Pick a small, scoped task

The [`good first issue`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues?q=is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) list is the first place to look — comment on one saying you'd like to take it. It's often thin, so these standing tasks are always open:

- **Add a detection.** New rules go under [`detections/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections) with positive *and* negative fixtures in [`detections/fixtures/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/detections/fixtures). Read [`detections/README.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/detections/README.md) first — it explains the four tiers and what "executable" means here (a rule replayed through the real engine and watched to fire, which is not the same as a rule that detects an attack).
- **Add a connector.** One Python class per source under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors). [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md) is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real one against a free no-auth API, so you can follow it without a vendor account. Requests and votes live in the [connector wishlist (#356)](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/issues/356).
- **Write a hunt.** Hunt-as-Code YAML hypotheses under [`hunts/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/hunts); [Hello, hunt](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/detections/hello-hunt.md) walks through one.
- **Add a playbook** under [`playbooks/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/playbooks).
- **Fix a typo or improve a doc page** under [`apps/docs/docs/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/apps/docs/docs).

## Step 3 — Make the change, open a PR

Commits need a sign-off (`git commit -s`); `git commit --amend -s --no-edit` fixes the last one and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes a branch.

The default [pull-request template](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md) walks you through what we need. The eval-harness section is required for substrate, playbook and detection changes — tick "Not applicable" otherwise.

Two things worth knowing before your first PR, because they're enforced and they surprise people:

- **Every published claim has to be true.** If you add a link it must resolve, and if you state a number it has to come from the tree rather than from memory. CI checks a lot of this.
- **No mock or fabricated data in the authenticated product.** Seeded and synthetic data is gated behind demo mode and labelled; honest empty and error states are the default everywhere else.

If you get stuck, [open a Q&A discussion](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/discussions/new?category=q-a) — don't suffer in silence.

The full contributor guide is [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and **Your first 30 minutes** near the top of it is a four-step version of this page.

Looking forward to your first PR. 🛡️

issues.title: Connector wishlist — what should AiSOC ingest next?
issues.body:
This is the rolling wishlist for **new connectors** the community would like to see ingested by AiSOC.

## How to vote / request

- 👍 the top comment for a connector you want.
- Reply with the *exact* product name + source format (REST? JSONL? syslog? S3 export?) + a link to the vendor's API docs. A signal score helps prioritisation: how many enterprises already rely on this in their SOC?
- If you've already shipped a custom connector for AiSOC, drop it here — even unmerged forks help.

## How to *build* one

**Start with [Hello, connector](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/hello-connector.md)** ([on the docs site](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors/hello-connector)). It is an end-to-end tutorial that builds a real, runnable connector against a free no-auth HTTP service, so you can walk every line of the contract — `schema()`, `test_connection()`, `fetch_alerts()`, `normalize()` and a smoke test — without a vendor account or an API key. [Connectors overview](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/docs/connectors/index.md) is the companion reference.

Connectors live under [`services/connectors/app/connectors/`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/tree/main/services/connectors/app/connectors), one Python class per source. The shape:

1. Subclass `BaseConnector` ([`base.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/base.py)) and declare a `schema()` returning a `ConnectorSchema` with the config fields your connector needs.
2. Pick a category. There are **nine**: `ai`, `cloud`, `edr`, `iam`, `ndr`, `network`, `saas`, `siem`, `vcs`.
3. Mark sensitive fields `secret=True` so the credential vault encrypts them at rest.
4. Register the class in `_CONNECTOR_CLASSES` **and `__all__`** in [`__init__.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py). Discovery is registry-based, so there is no other wiring — but two artefacts are derived from that tuple and both are `--check`-gated in CI, so regenerate and commit them or the build reds:
   ```bash
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py   # the "N connectors" claims
   python3 scripts/generate_connector_types.py   # the console's ConnectorType union
   ```
5. Add a marketplace manifest at `plugins/<connector-id>/plugin.yaml` mirroring `schema()`, then run `pnpm marketplace:sync`.
6. Preserve all five severity tiers in `normalize()` — `info | low | medium | high | critical`. If the vendor publishes a distinct `critical`, map it to `critical`; do not collapse it into `high`.
7. Nest the vendor payload under `raw_event` (not `raw`). The ingest normalizer's canonical-envelope check keys on that, and a connector that gets it wrong falls through to the generic profile, which is how events end up archived but never promoted to alerts.

Per-connector documentation pages under `apps/docs/docs/connectors/` are **generated** by [`scripts/generate_connector_docs.py`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/scripts/generate_connector_docs.py), which also owns the `Connectors` list in [`apps/docs/sidebars.ts`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/apps/docs/sidebars.ts) between its `GENERATED CONNECTOR LIST` markers — so run the generator rather than hand-editing the sidebar. A hand-written page wins over the generated one, but it still has to mention every required and secret field; the generator appends a marker-wrapped field reference to enforce that.

## Currently most-requested (auto-curated from comments)

_Maintainers will edit this list as votes pile up. PRs always welcome — the issue tracker is just the queue._

| Source | Category | Status |
|--------|----------|--------|
| _comments below feed this table_ |        |        |

## What already ships

**87 connectors** out of the box: 22 SaaS, 18 cloud, 17 SIEM, 10 EDR, 7 IAM, 7 network, 3 VCS, 2 NDR, 1 AI. The count is derived from the registry by `python3 scripts/generate_connector_count.py` and gated in CI, so check it there rather than trusting this paragraph.

The authoritative list is [`_CONNECTOR_CLASSES`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/services/connectors/app/connectors/__init__.py) or the [connectors overview](https://beenuar.github.io/AiSOC/docs/connectors). Not the marketplace — [`marketplace/index.json`](https://github.com/beenuar/AiSOC/blob/main/marketplace/index.json) carries **77** plugin manifests against those 84 registered connectors, so it undercounts. (A missing manifest for your connector is itself a reasonable first PR.)

If your tool isn't in the catalog and you don't want to write code, **universal capture** may already cover it — webhook URLs, an email relay, CEF syslog and Splunk HEC let any vendor that can POST or send mail land events in the same OCSF stream.

issues.title: [Bug] Dub turns unlisted language tags into another language (fil becomes Finnish, estonian becomes Spanish)
issues.body:
### Before filing

- [x] I searched existing issues and this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I'm on `main` (fc154e76).

### What happened?

Dub sets the wrong source language when a downloaded caption track or the remote ASR server reports a language code or name that is not in the dub allow-list. `detected_source_language` in `backend/services/dub_language.py` falls back to the first two letters of the value, and those letters are often a different language:

| Source | Value | Becomes | Language |
|---|---|---|---|
| YouTube caption track | `fil`, `fil-orig` | `fi` | Finnish instead of Filipino |
| YouTube caption track | `new` | `ne` | Nepali instead of Newari |
| YouTube caption track | `pam` | `pa` | Punjabi instead of Kapampangan |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `estonian` | `es` | Spanish |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `swedish` | `sw` | Swahili |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `kannada`, `kazakh` | `ka` | Georgian |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `armenian` | `ar` | Arabic |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `bengali` | `be` | Belarusian |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `tagalog` | `ta` | Tamil |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `latvian` | `la` | Latin |
| OpenAI-compatible ASR | `slovak` | `sl` | Slovenian |

Translation then runs from that wrong language, with no warning.

Supported languages get dropped too. They come back as "source language missing":

- YouTube's `iw` (Hebrew), `jv` (Javanese) and `yue-HK` (Cantonese).
- OpenAI names such as `spanish`, `german` and `portuguese`.

The OpenAI transcription API returns language names, for example `"language": "english"` in its `verbose_json` reference example. YouTube labels Filipino captions `fil` and Hebrew captions `iw`. I listed the codes from `yt-dlp -J` on a public video.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
cd backend && ../.venv/bin/python -c 'from services.dub_language import detected_source_language as d; [print(v, d(v)) for v in ["fil-orig", "estonian", "swedish", "yue-HK", "iw"]]'
```

Output on `main`:

```
fil-orig fi
estonian es
swedish sw
yue-HK None
iw None
```

In the app, the same thing happens when you dub a Filipino YouTube video and choose **Use downloaded captions**. `POST /dub/use-downloaded-captions/{job_id}` stores `source_lang = "fi"`, and translation treats the Filipino text as Finnish.

### What did you expect instead?

Each value should keep its own language (`fil` is `tl`, `estonian` is `et`, `yue-HK` is `yue`, `iw` is `he`) or come back as unknown. It should never become a different language. `services/pronunciation.py` fixed the same kind of two-letter cut in #2542.

### Operating system

All. The bug is in platform-independent backend code.

### How did you install it?

From source.

### Version

`main` at fc154e76.

### Compute device

Any. This is not related to the device.

### Active TTS/ASR engine

YouTube caption path: any engine. Remote path: OpenAI-compatible ASR.

issues.title: Local only can't be seen or turned off in the app, and its message tells users to run a command
issues.body:
With Local only on, the Agent UI blocks cloud models correctly, but the person can't see or change the setting in the app, and the message they get tells them to run a command: "Pick a local model. To allow cloud models again, run `gaia config set network_policy cloud_allowed`." The composer keeps offering the cloud model they can't use. In the Arabic UI the message is English.

Done when Local only is shown and switchable in Settings (with the same effects as the CLI), cloud models are marked as blocked in the pickers while it's on, and the refusal points to that setting in plain words, in English and Arabic.

**Steps (v0.25.4-rc8):** turn on Local only (`gaia config set network_policy local_ai_only`), open the Agent UI on a chat that used a Fireworks model, send a message.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

- The refusal is built in the backend (`local_only` message used by the agent's model-call error path) and shown verbatim.
- There is no Settings control for `network_policy`; the providers router and pickers don't read it.
- #5956 shipped the policy as CLI-first. Found in v0.25.4-rc8 release testing.
</details>

issues.title: Errors shown in the Agent UI still tell users to run gaia commands (and nothing checks for it)
issues.body:
Error messages that reach the Agent UI still tell desktop users to run GAIA commands: "Run `gaia init` to install it, then re-run the scheduled task", "run `gaia daemon status`", "Run `gaia gateway auth`", "run `gaia config set default_model <id>`" and about 20 more. A desktop user has no terminal habit and often no `gaia` on PATH, so these messages leave them stuck. #6686 removed the cases added since rc4; this covers the rest, and the check that stops new ones.

Done when:
- no message that can reach the Agent UI names a `gaia …` command (CLI-only paths may keep theirs);
- the UI shows a plain explanation with an in-app way forward;
- a test fails CI when such text is added.

<details>
<summary>🔍 Technical details</summary>

Examples on main: `src/gaia/ui/server.py` (scheduled task needs init), `src/gaia/llm/gateway.py` (`gaia gateway auth` ×6, `gaia config set default_model`), `src/gaia/llm/lemonade_client.py` (`gaia init` ×6, `gaia daemon status`), `src/gaia/llm/lemonade_launcher.py`, `lemonade_choice.SWITCH_BACK_HINT`.

Approach:
- Give errors a CLI remedy and a UI remedy, or attach a structured action code the UI maps to a button.
- Add a unit test that scans UI-reachable message builders and the webui locale files for `gaia <subcommand>` and fails outside an explicit CLI-only allowlist.

CLAUDE.md "No CLI remedies" has no automated check today, which is how F5/#6673 slipped in. Found in v0.25.4-rc8 release testing.
</details>

issues.title: Search page shows "No records found" despite backend returning matching cases
issues.body:
## Description

The Cases search page (`/cases/search/`) does not display any results in the UI, even though the backend successfully returns the data. The same records are visible and searchable through the Django admin panel (`/admin/`), confirming the data exists and is accessible.

This bug has been reproduced on **two independent Kiwi TCMS deployments** with the same migrated dataset, ruling out local environment issues.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Navigate to **Cases → Search** (`/cases/search/`)
2. Apply any filter (e.g. select a Product) or leave filters empty
3. Click **Search**

## Expected Behavior

The results table renders the matching test cases.

## Actual Behavior

- UI shows "No records found" / empty table / loading spinner
- Network tab in DevTools confirms the server **does return the matching records** in the response payload
- The same records are fully visible and searchable in Django admin at `/admin/testcases/testcase/`
- Reproduced consistently with and without filters, on multiple browsers

This indicates the issue is on the frontend rendering layer (likely DataTables), not the backend or database.

## Environment

Reproduced on **two separate deployments**:

**Deployment 1** — Local Docker
- Kiwi TCMS version: <!-- popuni -->
- Containers: `kiwi_web` + `kiwi_db` (MariaDB)
- OS: <!-- macOS / Linux -->

**Deployment 2** — Azure (fresh deploy)
- URL: `https://kiwi-vog7lvqxtaiok.eastus.cloudapp.azure.com/`
- Same Kiwi version, fresh database populated via the same API migration
- Confirms the bug is not environment-specific

**Common factors:**
- ~9,935 test cases in database
- Database populated via API migration from another test management system
- Browser: <!-- Chrome / Firefox / Safari + version -->

## Additional Context

- Server response time is fast (~500ms); response payload is large (~12MB when no filter is applied)
- Restarting the `kiwi_web` container does not resolve the issue
- Searching with narrow filters (specific Product) produces the same UI failure — records present in response, not displayed in UI
- No visible JavaScript error in Console; rendering simply never completes

## Workaround

Users must access cases via the Django admin panel, which is not viable for non-admin testers and defeats the purpose of the search feature.

## Possible Cause

The DataTables frontend appears to fail silently when processing larger JSON payloads. Possibly related to client-side rendering limits or a parsing error that does not surface as a console error.

## Suggested Fix

- Enforce server-side pagination on `/cases/search/` regardless of filter state
- Or surface a clear error message when client-side rendering fails
- Consider a hard cap on result-set size returned to the frontend, with a UI warning to refine filters

issues.title: Apostrophes are HTML-escaped in Test Run view when text is inside a YAML code block
issues.body:
### Description of problem
Text containing apostrophes is rendered inconsistently between the Test Case view and the Test Run execution view when the text is contained within a fenced YAML code block.

In the Test Case view, apostrophes are displayed correctly as '. However, when the same test case is executed within a Test Run, apostrophes inside the YAML code block are rendered as HTML entities (').

This causes the content displayed during test execution to differ from the content shown when viewing the test case.

### Version 
Kiwi TCMS 15.3
Kiwi TCMS 16.6-Enterprise DEMO

### Steps to Reproduce
https://public.tenant.kiwitcms.org/plan/16596/ - see the issue here

- Create or edit a test case.
- In the test case text, add a fenced YAML code block containing apostrophes:
```yaml
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
```
- Save the test case.
- Open the Test Case view and verify the content is rendered correctly.
- Add the test case to a Test Run or Plan and start execution.
- Observe the content displayed in the Test Run/Plan execution screen.

### Actual results
In the Test Case view:
```yaml
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
```
In the Test Run execution view:
```yaml
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
```

Apostrophes inside the YAML code block are HTML-escaped and displayed literally.

### Expected results
The content should be rendered identically in both views:
description: Access the user's profile page by clicking on the user's avatar
HTML entities should be decoded before rendering, including content inside fenced YAML code blocks.

### Additional info (Python traceback, logs, etc.)
The issue appears to be specific to fenced code blocks (tested with yaml). Regular text outside a code block renders correctly in both locations. The discrepancy is only observed when the text is displayed during Test Run/Plan execution.

issues.title: docs/mcp.md still says the repo is NVIDIA-internal and needs GitHub credentials, but it is public
issues.body:
## Summary

`docs/mcp.md` lines 47–51 still describe the repository as private:

> [!NOTE]
> Auto Ontology is NVIDIA-internal today, so this install needs GitHub credentials with
> access to the repository (`gh auth login`, or any cached git credential
> helper). It shortens to a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is published to
> PyPI; until then `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` alone will not resolve.

The repository is now public (`"visibility": "public"`), so the `uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp"` install no longer needs authenticated GitHub access. The second half of the note is still accurate: the package is not on PyPI, so plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` does not resolve.

The first half now reads as a gate that isn't there. A reader with no `gh` auth configured may reasonably assume the MCP server is unreachable and stop, when the documented command works as-is.

## Evidence

`docs/mcp.md` as of `main` today:

```
$ gh api repos/NVIDIA/auto-ontology/contents/docs/mcp.md --jq '.content' | base64 -d | sed -n '47,51p'
> [!NOTE]
> Auto Ontology is NVIDIA-internal today, so this install needs GitHub credentials with
> access to the repository (`gh auth login`, or any cached git credential
> helper). It shortens to a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is published to
> PyPI; until then `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` alone will not resolve.
```

Repository visibility:

```
$ gh api repos/NVIDIA/auto-ontology --jq '{visibility, private}'
{"visibility":"public","private":false}
```

The unauthenticated clone path resolves:

```
$ GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git /tmp/ao-check
Cloning into '/tmp/ao-check'...
remote: Enumerating objects: ...
```

## Suggested wording

The note can be shortened to the part that is still true:

> [!NOTE]
> The MCP package is not published to PyPI yet, so install it from the repository:
> `uvx --from "git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology.git#subdirectory=mcp" auto-ontology-mcp`.
> It shortens to a plain `uvx auto-ontology-mcp` once the package is published.

## Impact

Docs only. No code, no behavior change. Affects anyone following the MCP setup instructions from outside NVIDIA — which, with the repository public, is now the default audience.

Happy to leave this to the maintainers given `CONTRIBUTING.md` says external contributions are not being taken; filing it as a note rather than a patch for that reason.

issues.title: IRON JIT: support 1-overlay / N-sequence designs — separable insts/overlay compilation, parameterized (emitC) sequences, and a cache model that decouples them
issues.body:
### What are you trying to do?

The IRON JIT layer models a design as a single monolithic `(xclbin + insts)` artifact. This works for one-shot kernels, but not for a common pattern: **one shape-agnostic overlay driving many runtime sequences**, where the on-chip dataflow (tiles, ObjectFifos, kernels) is identical and only the shim runtime sequence differs. Today such designs must recompile the whole overlay for every sequence and discard the redundant xclbins.

This issue proposes closing that gap in three connected layers, from a minimal enabler up to the ergonomic goal.

### Layer (a) — allow insts-only / overlay-only compilation

`CompilableDesign.compile()` requires `xclbin_path` and `inst_path` to be set *together* (`python/aie/utils/compile/jit/compilabledesign.py:279`):

```python
if (xclbin_path is None) != (inst_path is None):
    raise ValueError("compile(): xclbin_path and inst_path must be set together ...")
```

But the underlying driver already gates the two artifacts independently (`python/aie/utils/compile/utils.py:478-481`):

```python
if insts_path:
    args.extend(["--get-npu-insts", f"--npu-insts-name={insts_path}"])
if xclbin_path:
    args.extend(["--get-xclbin", f"--xclbin-name={xclbin_path}"])
```

### Layer (b) — parameterized sequence as a standalone artifact (dynamic emitC path)

The runtime already has a **dynamic lowering path** (`python/aie/iron/runtime/runtime.py:8-15`): a sequence body with `range_`/`if_` and runtime scalar args lowers to `scf.for`/`scf.if` → **EmitC C++ TXN**, versus the static path (Python `range`/int bounds → flat binary insts). This is exactly the mechanism for "one sequence, shape supplied at launch" — instead of N static sequences, one parameterized sequence whose offsets/bounds are runtime values.

### Layer (c) — cache model that decouples overlay and sequence

The JIT cache is a single monolithic entry per `(recipe, device)` (`python/aie/utils/compile/jit/_hash.py:8-14`): `recipe_hash` (generator bytecode + `compile_kwargs` + flags) + `artifact_hash` (source/tool mtimes + device identity), materialized as one `<hash>/` dir holding `final.xclbin` + `insts.bin` **coupled**. There is no representation for "same overlay, different sequence," so a 1-overlay/N-seq design either bypasses the cache (explicit paths) or gets N full entries with duplicate overlays.

### Environment

- mlir-aie `1.4.0` (wheel), llvm-aie/Peano, NPU2 (Strix), Peano-only (no chess).

### Proposed solution

### Layer (a) — allow insts-only / overlay-only compilation

**Ask:** relax the check so **insts-only** (`inst_path` given, `xclbin_path=None`) and **overlay-only** (the reverse) are valid modes, threading through only the relevant `--get-*` flag. Backward-compatible — existing callers pass both.

This alone lets a caller build the overlay once and emit N sequences against it manually.

### Layer (b) — parameterized sequence as a standalone artifact (dynamic emitC path)

**Ask:** make the dynamic/parameterized runtime sequence a **first-class standalone artifact** that (a) enables. Combined, this turns our 20 static `.seq.bin` into **one overlay + one parameterized sequence**. This is the actual capability; layer (a) is its packaging.

### Layer (c) — cache model that decouples overlay and sequence

**Ask:** allow the cache to key the **overlay** and the **sequence(s)** separately — an overlay entry keyed on the dataflow/recipe, and sequence entries keyed on `(overlay-hash, sequence-params)` — so the pattern is cache-ergonomic, not merely possible. This is the design question underlying (a) and (b); without it the feature works but re-derives the overlay hash coupling.

### Suggested increments

- [ ] (a) Relax `compile()` to permit insts-only / overlay-only. *(minimal, self-contained)*
- [ ] (b) Expose the dynamic emitC sequence as a standalone, overlay-decoupled artifact.
- [ ] (c) Cache model keying overlay and sequence(s) independently.

(a) is independently useful and low-risk; (b)+(c) deliver the ergonomic 1-overlay/N-sequence (or 1-overlay/1-parameterized-sequence) goal.

issues.title: [P2][fsutil] FileLock 超时分支不关文件句柄（strict 抛 TimeoutError 时 fd 泄漏）
issues.body:
## 现象

`md_cg/fsutil.py` 的 `FileLock.__enter__` 在 **strict 超时分支直接 `raise TimeoutError`，没有关闭已打开的文件句柄**。

```python
def __enter__(self):
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or ".", exist_ok=True)
    self._f = open(self.path, "a+b")          # ← 打开
    deadline = time.time() + self.timeout
    while True:
        try:
            if IS_WIN:
                self._f.seek(0)
                msvcrt.locking(self._f.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
            else:
                fcntl.flock(self._f.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            self.acquired = True
            return self
        except OSError as e:
            if e.errno not in (errno.EACCES, errno.EAGAIN, errno.EDEADLK):
                raise
            if time.time() > deadline:
                if self.strict:
                    raise TimeoutError(f"FileLock 超时未获锁（strict）：{self.path}")   # ← 没有 self._f.close()
                return self          # 放行，不阻断写路径
            time.sleep(self.poll)
```

**两个泄漏点**：
1. `raise TimeoutError(...)` 前没有 `self._f.close()`（`__exit__` 不会被调用，因为 `__enter__` 抛异常）；
2. 第 16 行 `raise`（非 EACCES/EAGAIN/EDEADLK 的错误，例如 ENOENT/EIO）同样不关。

## 影响

- 高竞争路径上每次 strict 超时**累积一个泄漏的 fd**；
- Windows 上 `msvcrt.locking` 的锁随 fd 关闭释放 —— **泄漏的 fd 持锁不释放**？需确认（`msvcrt.locking` 锁的是字节范围，fd 关才释放）；
- 长跑进程（DSH 常驻、serve 实例）里可能逐步耗尽句柄。

## 实测状态（重要：**未能触发**）

在 Windows 上构造「一个线程持锁 + 另一线程 strict timeout=0.2」**没有超时**（竞争线程拿到了锁）：
```
持锁线程已进入
竞争线程结果: got        ← 期望 TimeoutError，实际拿到锁
```
⇒ **Windows 的 `msvcrt.locking` 在同一进程内的不同 fd 之间不互斥**（或本实现另有进程内路径）。
⇒ 要触发必须**跨进程**。

## 建议修法

```python
            if time.time() > deadline:
                if self.strict:
                    self._f.close()          # 先关
                    self._f = None
                    raise TimeoutError(f"FileLock 超时未获锁（strict）：{self.path}")
                return self
```
同理第 16 行的 `raise` 也要先关（或整段包 `try/finally`）。

## 关联

本 issue 是核 issue #732（覆写重置元数据）时，验证单元读代码发现的**副产品**，与 #732 无因果关系。
若 #732 后续给 `MdCG.add` 加节点锁（`node_write_lock` 内部就用 `FileLock(strict=True)`），
超时路径会变高频，这条就更值得修。

issues.title: [P2][索引] _stage 与 rebuild_index 的 content_hash 不同源（同节点同正文两个值）
issues.body:
## 现象

**同一条节点、同一份正文**，`_stage` 写入索引的 `content_hash` 与 `rebuild_index` 重算出来的**不一样**。

实测（本机临时库，`MdCGOS`）：
```
首写后（_stage 定向 upsert）  content_hash = 9eb1d121c59f
rebuild_index() 之后           content_hash = aaf2ffbbdd36      ← 不同！

只改 fm（importance 0.5→0.9，正文逐字不变）后再 rebuild:
  aaf2ffbbdd36 → aaf2ffbbdd36                                ← rebuild 口径与 fm 无关 ✓

改正文后再 rebuild:
  aaf2ffbbdd36 → 5f02f6b50bdd                                ← rebuild 口径跟正文走 ✓
```

## 影响

1. **「写入后」与「重建后」的 `content_hash` 不同源** —— 这正是仓内 **N137「重建后有、写入后没有」形态**的镜像；
2. 任何用 `content_hash` 做「内容是否变化 / 是否陈旧 / 去重」判断的路径，在**写完但未重建**的窗口里会判错；
3. `nodefile.content_hash` 的 docstring 明写「**只哈希正文，不含 frontmatter**」并强调「两处共用且必须逐位一致，否则对账/变更探测会永远『匹配成功』而失去意义」—— 现在两处**不一致**。

## 未核实的部分（诚实标注）

- **`_stage` 侧的口径没测到**：因为 `_stage` 是**定向 upsert**，若它交的 dict 里没带 `content_hash`，`_set_index_entry` 会**保留旧值** ⇒「改 fm 后 hash 没变」这个读数与该口径无关；
- 未定位两处计算代码（`_stage` 约 `mdcg.py:3667-3725`，`rebuild` 走 `_node_entry` 约 `2853-2930`），**未判定**是「算法输入面不同」还是「同一算法两种实现」。

## 建议（定位串）

```
grep -n "content_hash" md_cg/nodefile.py md_cg/mdcg.py md_cg/mdcos.py
grep -n "def _stage\|def _node_entry\|def rebuild_index" md_cg/*.py
```
判定标准：两处若一处传「正文」、另一处传「正文 + fm/整文件/封装后字节」，即**输入面不同**；
若都传同一参数但规范化（strip / 换行 / slot 渲染）不同，即**同一算法两种实现**。

## 关账标准

补一条守卫：**同一节点在「写入后」与 `rebuild_index()` 后，`content_hash` 必须相等**。
（这条在 `_stage` 漏带 `content_hash` 时也会红 —— 那本身就是缺陷。）

## 关联

本 issue 是核 #732 时用 `rebuild_index` 做判别实验的**副产品**，与 #732 无因果关系。

issues.title: scrub._contradiction 分支二：六要素模板头 + 不适用条件让任意 CCG 节点互判矛盾（#726 残留）
issues.body:
## 现象

`scrub` 自主 sweep 把语义无关、各自合法的 CCG 节点判为「极性相反且共享内容」，落盘 weaken 后 demote（knowledge → contextual）。本机 0.9.21 上共有 12 个 knowledge 节点被降级，且每小时重复追加同一条 weakened 证据。

#726 记录过同族问题（当时分支一「同键不同值」已修），本报告是剩下的分支二：`极性相反且共享 bigram`。

## 根因

`md_cg/scrub.py` 的 `_contradiction()` 用**全文**计算 `bigrams()` 和 `_polarity()`：

1. 六要素模板头（`# 功能名：` `# 生效条件：` `# 子功能：` `# 执行：` `# 验证方式：` `# 不适用条件：`）每个节点都有，单这部分就贡献 20+ 个共享 bigram，`len(shared) >= 3 and ratio >= 0.15` 几乎必过。
2. `# 不适用条件：` 按定义写拒绝域，天然含 `_NEG_WORDS`（不要/不得/避免…），而另一节点正文里只要出现一个 `_POS_WORDS`（可以/需要/建议…）就判为极性相反。

两条叠加 ⇒ 任意两条 CCG 节点都可能被判矛盾。

## 最小复现（0.9.21）

```python
from md_cg import scrub
A = """# 功能名：billion-context 压缩代理配置
# 生效条件：调整 DSH 上下文压缩代理
# 子功能：配置文件热加载
# 执行：用 acp_status 查看
# 验证方式：代理自估 token 数高于上游
# 不适用条件：不要把代理估算值当作上游计费值"""
B = """# 功能名：部署链失败即停
# 生效条件：执行部署步骤
# 子功能：先 disconnect 再 reconnect
# 执行：部署写成 set -e 脚本
# 验证方式：可以核验 /ready
# 不适用条件：只读查询类命令串"""

class CG:
    def get(self, i): return {"content": B}

print(scrub._polarity(A), scrub._polarity(B))          # -1 1
print(scrub._contradiction(CG(), A, [{"node_id": "b"}]))  # 判为矛盾：共享片段 26 个
```

## 建议修法（本机已用 pnpm patch 验证）

比对前只取「主张正文」：剥掉六要素标题前缀，整行去掉 `不适用条件`，再算 bigram 与极性。

```python
def _claim_body(content) -> str:
    out = []
    for raw in (content or "").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        head = line.lstrip("#").strip()
        mark = next((m for m in nodefile.CCG_MARKS if head.startswith(m)), None)
        if mark is None:
            out.append(line); continue
        if mark == "不适用条件":
            continue
        out.append(head[len(mark):].lstrip("：:").strip())
    return "\n".join(out)
```

`_contradiction` 中 `bigrams(content)` / `_polarity(content)` 与对端 `oc` 两处都改为作用于 `_claim_body(...)`。

## 验证

守卫（原版红、补丁后绿）：
- 上面 A/B 两条无关节点 → `None`
- 真矛盾仍检出：`# 执行：可以手改 nft 规则管理防火墙端口` vs `# 执行：不要手改 nft 规则管理防火墙端口` → 非 `None`
- `_claim_body(A)` 不含 `功能名`、不含 `不要`，保留 `acp_status`

回归：`test_p15_scrub` 53/53、`test_issue444_scrub_evidence_plaintext` 10/10、`test_issue665_scrub_process_records` 4/4。

## 附带

已被误降级的节点没有单点恢复路径：`verify(confirmed)` 能把 doubted → verified，但层留在 contextual；`consolidate promote` 是按热度批量扫描，不接受指定 node_id。建议补一个「撤销 scrub 误降级」的定向回滚。

issues.title: [enhancement] 增加拟人感、防止刷屏的回复模式设计
issues.body:
# 目标

- 通过简单的逻辑和实现方式来配置表情的延迟和带图的回复模式，有效增加bot发送表情包时的拟人感。
- 以及有效防止各种情境下的刷屏

---

是否启用延迟发表情（仅对非“回复带图”场景生效）

```yaml
enable_delayed_dispatch: true
```

## 消息分类策略

可以设计一组**互斥的概率策略参数**，支持三种模式：

1. **auto（默认）**
   不设置概率

   * 短消息：100% inline
   * 长消息：100% 延迟表情

2. **global_probability（统一概率）**
   所有消息统一概率触发表情

3. **separate_probability（长短消息分别概率）**
   分别配置短消息与长消息概率

下面是一份**结构清晰且兼容当前配置的示例**：

```yaml
emotion_dispatch:

  # =========================
  # 概率策略
  # =========================

  # auto | global | separate
  # auto:
  #   短消息 100% 带图
  #   长消息 100% 不带图
  #
  # global:
  #   所有消息统一概率
  #
  # separate:
  #   分别设置短消息和长消息概率
  probability_mode: auto


  # =========================
  # 统一概率模式
  # =========================

  # 仅在 probability_mode = global 时生效
  # 表情触发概率 (0.0 - 1.0)
  emotion_probability: 0.35


  # =========================
  # 分离概率模式
  # =========================

  # 仅在 probability_mode = separate 时生效

  # 短消息带图概率
  short_message_probability: 0.9

  # 长消息带图概率
  long_message_probability: 0.25
```

逻辑：

```python
if probability_mode == "auto":
    if short_message:
        send_emotion = True
    else:
        send_emotion = False

elif probability_mode == "global":
    send_emotion = random() < emotion_probability

elif probability_mode == "separate":
    if short_message:
        send_emotion = random() < short_message_probability
    else:
        send_emotion = random() < long_message_probability
```


## 延迟计算参数
```
# 基础延迟

base_delay_ms: 900


# 每个字符增加的延迟
# 用于模拟用户的阅读速度，读完再发个表情

delay_per_char_ms: 10ms

# 最小延迟限制/最大延迟限制

min_delay_ms: 700 / max_delay_ms: 3500


# 随机扰动范围 最终延迟会增加 [-jitter, +jitter] 的随机值

delay_jitter_ms: 300
```

## 防刷屏控制

表情发送冷却时间
在该时间内不会再次发送表情
可以缓解因为群聊与bot聊天消息较少、所以设置的触发概率较高、但又避免某个时间段连续发很多表情的情况。

```yaml
cooldown_seconds: 20
```

## 防抖机制

如果延迟期间用户再次 @bot
是否取消本次待发送表情

```yaml
cancel_on_user_followup: true
```

监听用户追问的时间窗口
此项配置在群内多个人@bot时能有效防止表情包刷屏
在此时间内Bot被其他用户@取消发送表情包，改为下一次必定触发。

```yaml
cancel_on_user_followup_delay_ms: 1000
```

issues.title: hermes gateway status falsely warns "did not restart running gateways" forever — served_profiles schema mismatch
issues.body:
### Summary
After a genuine, verified `hermes gateway restart` (new PID, `code_sha` matching `git rev-parse HEAD` exactly, fresh boot log showing all profiles ticking), `hermes gateway status` / `hermes update` keep printing:

```
⚠ A previous `hermes update` pulled new code but did not restart running gateways.
  Gateways may still be serving pre-update modules (mixed sys.modules).
```

This never clears, even after multiple full restarts.

### Root cause
The live gateway's `identify` control-socket response (`gateway/control_socket.py::build_identify_payload`) now returns `served_profiles` as a list of **dicts**:
```json
"served_profiles": [{"profile_id": "/Users/.../profiles/accountant", "home": "..."}, ...]
```

But `hermes_cli/update_receipt.py::_fleet_row()` validates it with:
```python
if isinstance(served_profiles, list) and served_profiles and all(
    isinstance(name, str) and name for name in served_profiles
):
    row["served_profiles"] = list(dict.fromkeys(served_profiles))
```
This expects `list[str]` (the old format). Against the new `list[dict]` shape, `all(isinstance(name, str) ...)` is `False`, so the field is dropped entirely — the comment says "corrupt status must not widen coverage", but this isn't corrupt, it's just a newer shape the validator doesn't know about.

Downstream, `hermes_cli/update_cmd_fleet.py::_fleet_covered_gateways()` then only credits `("gateway", "default")`, so every other profile served by the same multiplexed process (confirmed live and correct via the gateway's own boot log: `Cron scheduler will tick 10 profile(s)`) is permanently treated as "not yet restarted" — hence the warning never clears.

### Reproduction
```python
from gateway.control_socket import identify_gateway
from pathlib import Path
print(identify_gateway(Path.home() / ".hermes"))
# served_profiles is list[dict], not list[str]

from hermes_cli.update_receipt import collect_fleet_versions
from hermes_cli.update_cmd_fleet import _fleet_covered_gateways
rows = collect_fleet_versions()
print(_fleet_covered_gateways(rows))
# {('gateway', 'default')} — only one profile credited out of 10
```

### Expected fix
Update `_fleet_row()`'s validation to accept the current `served_profiles` shape (extract `profile_id`/`home` from each dict, or whatever the canonical identifier is) instead of requiring plain strings. Likely same fix needed anywhere else in the codebase that still assumes `served_profiles: list[str]`.

### Environment
Hermes v0.22.5+3299.ga7b8d34, macOS, multiplexed default gateway serving 10 profiles, launchd-supervised.

issues.title: Context engines that subclass ContextCompressor are dropped as "built-in" on the gateway /compress path
issues.body:
After #145806 (`aad60e1`), `gateway/session_mutation_compress.py::_plugin_engine()` decides whether to use the session's configured engine like this:

```python
return None if engine is None or isinstance(engine, ContextCompressor) else engine
```

Any engine that subclasses `ContextCompressor` is treated as the built-in compressor, so `prepare_compress()` falls through and constructs a fresh `ContextCompressor(...)`. That is correct for engines that implement `ContextEngine` from scratch, but `ContextCompressor` is itself a legitimate base class for a plugin engine.

A plugin can override only the summary-generation internals — `_generate_summary` as the entry point, plus `_synthesize`, the budget/trim helpers and the section merge — and reuse everything else from the base: `compress()`, `should_compress()`, `update_from_response()`, head/tail protection, the DB write-back and the failure cooldowns. That is a far smaller and more maintainable plugin than reimplementing the compression pipeline, and it stays in sync with upstream behaviour changes for free.

I hit this on v0.22.5. The engine overrides 15 private methods and leaves all four `ContextEngine` abstract methods to the base class. With the #145806 patch applied, `/compress` from the desktop app on a gateway-backed session still ran the built-in compressor: `_plugin_engine()` returned `None`, `prepare_compress()` built a new `ContextCompressor`, and the plugin never executed. Nothing was logged at warning level — the only observable signal was the absence of the plugin's own log lines, which made this hard to distinguish from "the plugin is broken".

Suggested fix — compare exact types rather than subclasses:

```python
return None if engine is None or type(engine) is ContextCompressor else engine
```

Or key off the engine registry that produced the instance rather than its type. The same `isinstance` pattern appears in two more places in the file (the `owned=` argument to `engine_owner`, and the `compressed is None` cleanup path), so all three need the same treatment to stay consistent.

**Repro**

1. Register a `ContextEngine` whose class inherits `ContextCompressor` and overrides only `_generate_summary`.
2. Set `context.engine` to it.
3. Run `/compress` from the desktop app on a gateway-backed session.
4. Observe the built-in compressor running: its `Detailed Session Log` / `Anchor Index` sections appear instead of the plugin's own format, and none of the plugin's log lines are emitted.

Pre-#145806 the plugin was bypassed on this route unconditionally; post-#145806 it is still dropped, because the exclusion check now catches it by type.

issues.title: verify(verdict=weakened, override=True) 对受保护节点仍被拒：override 未透传到 set_verification
issues.body:
## 现象

对一个 `importance ≥ 0.7` 的受保护知识节点做「证据被削弱」裁决，**显式给出 `override=True` 仍然被拒**：

```
cg(op="verify", node_id="mem_…", verdict="weakened", override=True, evidence="…")
→ {
    "action": "weakened",
    "confidence": 0.3,
    "verification": {
      "from": "unverified", "to": "doubted",
      "code": "protected", "ok": false, "error": "protected",
      "reason": "受保护节点不接受降级迁移 unverified→doubted（保护 = 不可轻弃）；确需降级请显式 override=True"
    }
  }
```

注意提示语本身就在说「请显式 override=True」，而调用方**已经**给了。

## 定位

`md_cg/mdcg.py`（0.9.21，`verify()` 在 6107 行起）的 weakened 分支：

```python
else:
    ver = self.set_verification(
        node_id, "doubted",
        reason=f"外部裁决 weakened：{str(evidence)[:80]}",
        actor="verify:weakened", evidence=evidence, trigger="verify")   # ← 少了 override=override
```

而 `set_verification`（3755 行）是**支持**这个参数的：

```python
def set_verification(self, node_id, dst, reason=None, actor=None, evidence=None,
                     method=None, trigger=None, override: bool = False) -> dict:
    return trust.set_state(..., override=override)
```

对照 `falsified` 分支：它经 `protect.guard_forget(self, node_id, override=override, ...)`，override 是**透传的**（实测：不带 override 被 `ProtectionError` 拒，带上就真的从 `trash/` 删除）。所以这是 weakened 分支单独漏了一行，不是全局设计。

## 后果（比这一行更值得看）

受保护节点因此**没有「降级 / 存疑」通道**，只剩两个出口：

| 出口 | 效果 | 问题 |
|---|---|---|
| `confirmed` | unverified → verified | 只能让它更像对的 |
| `falsified` | 软删进 `trash/` | 语义是「这条是假的」，而「被新事实取代」不是假 |

我这次的实际处境：库里 12 条知识有 11 条 `importance ≥ 0.7`（自动保护），其中 3 条是**曾经正确、后来被取代**的配置记录。它们不该被判为「假」（falsified 对受保护节点一次 override 就真删），也不能被 `confirmed`。结果是这 3 条只能保持 `unverified` 原样挂着 —— **审计能发现它们过时，但工具没有地方记这个结论**。

这也解释了一个可观测的库面现象：`cg(op=status)` 里 135 个节点 `verification_state` 只有 `unverified` / `verified`，`doubted` 恒为 0。不是没人怀疑过，是**怀疑写不进去**。

## 建议

1. 最小修复：weakened 分支补 `override=override`，与 confirmed/falsified 三条出口对齐。
2. 更希望有第三态：现在 `falsified` = 删除，缺一个「**已被取代 / superseded**」—— 保留节点、标注取代者与取代时间，让历史证据不被抹掉。`_link.jsonl` 的 `merged_from` / `refined_from` 已能表达血缘，差一个"本节点不再作为当前状态引用"的验证态。

## 复现

```
1. 建一个 importance=0.7 及以上的 knowledge 节点（会自动打 protected 标记，fm 里能看到 protection_reason）
2. cg(op="verify", node_id=<它>, verdict="weakened", override=True, evidence="任意")
3. 返回体 verification.code == "protected"，节点 verification_state 不变
4. 把 override 去掉再跑一次 —— 返回完全一样
```

第 4 步是关键：**带与不带 override 结果逐字相同**，这排除了「别处还有第二道闸」的可能。

## 边界

- 未受保护节点（importance < 0.7）可以正常 weakened，问题只在受保护节点上；
- 只测了 MCP 的 `cg(op=verify)` 这一条入口，没测 `insight verify` / `verify_record`；
- 结论基于 0.9.21，且比对过仓库 `main`（`md_cg/mdcg.py` 6107 行起这段与本地逐行相同），未修。

环境：dsh-memory 0.9.21，Windows 11，DSH 桌面版。

issues.title: Is skipping de-risk when a rebuy lacks available margin intentional?
issues.body:
Hi,

Could you clarify the intended priority between rebuy and de-risk when there is insufficient margin for another entry?

We checked X7 **v17.5.169** (`short_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v3`) and X8 **v18.0.137** (`short_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v4`). The same behavior remains in X7 v17.5.171 and X8 v18.0.140 at commit `c726393`.

When the rebuy conditions pass, the following check returns from the entire adjustment function:

```python
if buy_amount > max_stake:
    return None
```

The de-risk check is located later in the same function, so it is never evaluated in that call—even if its loss threshold has already been exceeded.

Source: [X7](https://github.com/iterativv/NostalgiaForInfinity/blob/c7263935a83b97ed7baa6b8ae0c02741ebe4ae2b/NostalgiaForInfinityX7.py#L79268), [X8](https://github.com/iterativv/NostalgiaForInfinity/blob/c7263935a83b97ed7baa6b8ae0c02741ebe4ae2b/NostalgiaForInfinityX8.py#L61535).

A synthetic short-position example:

- Leverage: **3×**.
- First entry: **1,200 USDT notional / 400 USDT margin**.
- One rebuy has already filled.
- Current P&L: approximately **−607 USDT**.
- Rebuy de-risk threshold: **−560 USDT** (`400 × −1.40`).
- All conditions for the next rebuy pass, but available margin is **zero**.

The callback returns `None`. With the same position, P&L and available margin, making one rebuy indicator condition false allows execution to reach de-risk and return a negative adjustment tagged `derisk_level_3`. We reproduced this with isolated callback tests in both strategies.

**Is holding the position intentional while rebuy conditions remain valid, even when the rebuy cannot be funded? Or should an unaffordable rebuy allow the function to continue to the de-risk check?**

Your clarification would help us distinguish the intended trading policy from an unintended control-flow interaction. We have left the strategy unchanged.

issues.title: Rebuy mode v3/v4: rebuys 3 and 4 can't fire before rebuy de-risk at 3x or in spot. Intended?
issues.body:
Hi, this is a question rather than a bug report.

X8 at `5bbcf197a` has these settings (X7 `system_v3_*` has the same):

```python
system_v4_rebuy_mode_stakes_futures = [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
system_v4_rebuy_mode_thresholds_futures = [-0.08, -0.12, -0.16, -0.20]
system_v4_rebuy_mode_derisk_futures = -1.40
system_v4_rebuy_mode_derisk_spot = -0.48
```

In `long_rebuy_adjust_trade_position_v4`, each rebuy is one first-entry slice. It fires when the price is the threshold below the last entry. Rebuy de-risk fires when `profit_stake < slice_amount * derisk / leverage`.

Take the shallowest possible path, where each rebuy fills exactly at its threshold. In units of the first entry's notional:

| rebuy | price vs first entry | loss when price reaches it | can fire before de-risk only if |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.920 | 0.080 | leverage ≤ 17.5 |
| 2 | 0.810 | 0.310 | leverage ≤ 4.5 |
| 3 | 0.680 | 0.741 | leverage ≤ 1.89 |
| 4 | 0.544 | 1.393 | leverage ≤ 1.0 |

So at the default `futures_mode_leverage = 3.0`, and in spot (0.48 < 0.741), rebuys 3 and 4 can never fire. A deeper path only makes the loss larger. De-risk fires about 6% below the price of rebuy 2.

Backtest check: Binance futures, 3x, 2024-01 to 2026-10, volume top-90 pairlist. Of 603 long rebuy-mode trades, 498 had 0 rebuys, 92 had 1, 13 had 2 and none had a third.

History: on 2025-11-14 the thresholds were widened from `[-0.04, -0.06, -0.08, -0.10]` to `[-0.08, -0.12, -0.16, -0.20]` (X7 3d5ce9a5d, 71c28d530). The rebuy stop stayed at 1.40 and later became the de-risk level (c11c7c557).

Is "first entry + 2 rebuys, then de-risk" the intended design? If so, trimming the arrays to two rebuys would make that explicit. If four rebuys are intended, the de-risk level and the thresholds don't fit together at 3x.

I'm not proposing a behaviour change, only asking whether this is intended.

issues.title: RG CubeXX: gmloader ports fail at SDL init (no haptic) because mod.txt's -c heuristic forces the vendor SDL2
issues.body:
### Bug report code

_No response_

### Device

Anbernic RG CubeXX

### spruce version

4.5.4

### What happened?

Downwell (PortMaster, gmloader-next) hangs on the loading splash and ignores all input except Menu+Start. log.txt ends with:

  gmloader/main.cpp:257: SDL could not initialize! SDL_Error: SDL not built with haptic (force feedback) support

Cause:
In /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/portmaster/mod.txt, this check runs against the launch script:

  grep -qE '\$GPTOKEYB2?[^&|;]*[[:space:]]-c[[:space:]]' "$0"

Downwell.sh contains `$GPTOKEYB "gmloadernext.aarch64" -c "downwell.gptk" &`, so it matches and /mnt/SDCARD/spruce/h700/lib64/sdl2 is prepended to LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The port ships no SDL2 of its own, so gmloader loads that build, which has no haptic support, and gmloader requires it. The -c flag only means "use this config file", so the heuristic matches nearly every gptokeyb port, not just keyboard-driven ones.

Workaround that fixed it:
Added this to Downwell.sh after get_controls:

  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="/mnt/SDCARD/App/PyUI/dll-mali:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH#/mnt/SDCARD/spruce/h700/lib64/sdl2:}"

The game launches and input works afterward, so the dll-mali SDL2 also works with gptokeyb for this port.

Suggestion:
Exempt gmloader ports from the vendor-SDL2 branch (for example, skip it when the script launches gmloadernext), or ship a vendor SDL2 built with haptic enabled.

issues.title: SM8350 (Xiaomi star) port from ios-sweet: early undefined-instruction panic after GIC init — any guidance from the 8 Gen 2 work?
issues.body:
I'm porting to an **SM8350** device (Xiaomi `star` / Mi 11 Ultra, 8 GB) starting from `ios-sweet`,
with `ios-v60` (SM8250) as the reference. Full write-up with logs and everything I ruled out is in
dipa-studio/ios-sweet#14, so I won't duplicate it here.

Short version: the kernel gets through framebuffer + GIC init, then panics with

```
SWEET GIC: virtual timer INTID 27
panic(cpu 0 caller 0xfffffe0007a6d490): Undefined kernel instruction: pc=0xfffffe0007a6e878
instr=0x51ba228  sleh.c:351
```

and the panic immediately nests (`Original panic string:` / `Nested panic count exceeds limit 5`),
so the printed `pc`/`instr` look corrupted: that pc resolves to `IOHIDEvent::proximityEvent+0xc8`,
whose instruction in the image is a plain `mov`.

You went from a 7-series-era tree to **8 Gen 2**, which is the same "newer Qualcomm" direction I'm
going. Two questions:

1. Did you hit anything similar right after GIC init on the newer SoCs, and what was it?
   (An Apple IMPDEF register still reachable on the early path? A required DT node I'm missing?)
2. Is there a device-tree node/property your board files carry that `ios-sweet`'s `mkadt.py` does not,
   which the newer Qualcomm platforms need before interrupts work?

I can boot any test image on the device freely (it's a spare) and report numbers back.

issues.title: fuxi: reaches userland, but GPU switches trap userland; a clean clone cannot build the kernel (xnu-prelink candidates missing)
issues.body:
## Summary

On Xiaomi 13 (fuxi, SM8550, A740) with `UniXNU@main` + `ljhhkx529/unixnu-fuxi@old`
+ `ljhhkx529/uefi-fuxi@old`, the port already reaches userland:

- display (GOP/PM4) and VM up
- UFS reads the userdata windows (24 万 requests), APFS root mounts, Apple logo shows
- diagnostics list `PROC backboardd` / `PROC SpringBoard`

Two things block further progress, and I would like to know whether they are
expected inputs I am missing, or bugs.

## 1. Any GPU switch kills userland processes

| kernel_args GPU subset | result |
| --- | --- |
| none | ✅ Apple logo, launchd, backboardd, SpringBoard (SpringBoard then exits with NSException) |
| `sheng-fb-gpu=1 sheng-vsync=120` | ❌ black screen, `status=exited sig=5` |

| full set (adds `sheng-gpu-dcvs`, `sheng-gpu-power=9`) | ❌ kernel `IRQ-off hard lock` |

Diagnostics excerpt:

```
EXIT p229 live/activated status=exited sig=5 exited=0 ne2 sub=5
PROC backboardd p56 ...
PROC SpringBoard p27 ...
FS: total verif=3419ms read=2115ms req=249784
```

`sig=5` looks like a trap after Metal device creation fails.

Also, the device repo pins `qcom/sm8550/fuxi/a740_zap.mbn` as 9,040 bytes /
`e05d28dd…`, while the ZAP extracted from this phone's ODM partition is
12,088 bytes / `fd107982…`. Which one does the A740 path expect?

## 2. A clean clone cannot build the kernel

On `macos-26` + Xcode 26.6 (the `macOS build` workflow), against
`ljhhkx529/unixnu-fuxi@old`:

1. `archive-11-build-sheng-platform-power` fails with

2. For a board that still uses a board-local driver (`NativeAdreno`), is the

   Does the shared component carry the board's firmware selection?
3. Would you accept a patch that makes `pre_build` able to stage the stage-2a
   candidate so the CI can build a board whose archive chain needs it?

issues.title: Show Texture shows white screen for large models on Windows with Node.js v24
issues.body:
How did you install WebODM (docker, installer, etc.)?

  Windows installer, version 3.2.8

  What's your browser and operating system? (Copy/paste the output of https://www.whatismybrowser.com/)

Chrome 152 on Windows 11

[glbopti.js](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31883499/glbopti.js)

  What is the problem?

  Clicking "Show Texture" on the 3D model view shows a white screen for any task whose GLB output exceeds 150 MB. CPU briefly spikes, the progress bar moves, then
  the model area goes blank. Smaller models display correctly.

  glbopti.js (which optimizes large GLBs before browser delivery) fails to load because of a broken native binary bundled in a transitive dependency. The
  dependency chain is:

  @gltf-transform/functions → ndarray-pixels → ndarray-pixels/node_modules/sharp@0.35.4
      → ndarray-pixels/node_modules/@img/sharp-win32-x64/sharp-win32-x64-0.35.4.node

  That .node binary fails with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED: The specified procedure could not be found under Node.js v24 on Windows. Because it is loaded eagerly at module
  level, require('@gltf-transform/functions') throws before main() runs, causing glbopti.js to exit with an error. task.py catches the failure and falls back to
  serving the raw unoptimized GLB, which is too large for the browser to render — hence the white screen.

  A secondary issue: even after working around the load crash, compressTexture() from @gltf-transform/functions triggers a libvips error on ODM-generated textures:

  GLib-GObject-CRITICAL: value "32" of type 'gint' is invalid or out of range for property 'space' of type 'VipsInterpretation'
  Error: colourspace: parameter space not set

  This is caused by getTextureColorSpace() returning a value that leads libvips 8.15.3 (bundled with sharp 0.33.5) into an invalid colorspace conversion path.

  How can we reproduce this? (What steps trigger the problem? What parameters are you using for processing? Does it work with the default settings? Include
  screenshots. If you are having issues processing a dataset, you must include a copy of your dataset uploaded on Dropbox, Google Drive or https://dronedb.app)

  1. Run WebODM on Windows with Node.js v24
  2. Process any dataset that produces a GLB larger than 150 MB
  3. Click "Show Texture" on the 3D model view → white screen

  Fix: Two changes to app/scripts/glbopti.js resolve both issues:

  1. Delete node_modules/ndarray-pixels/node_modules/ so ndarray-pixels falls back to the top-level compatible sharp 0.33.5 instead of its bundled incompatible
  0.35.4 binary.
  2. Replace the compressTexture() call with direct sharp calls (texture.getImage() → resize → .jpeg() → texture.setImage()), bypassing the broken colorspace
  detection path.

  A corrected glbopti.js is attached. After applying it and deleting app/scripts/node_modules/ndarray-pixels/node_modules/, a 567 MB GLB with three 24576×24576
  textures processes and displays correctly.

issues.title: [Feature]  Explicitly requested tasks
issues.body:
## Problem / motivation

Explicitly requested tasks are currently handled through alert evaluation. A request can receive a “Created” response after being submitted for evaluation, without a persistent task being saved or appearing in “Needs you.”

This makes it difficult to determine whether a task exists, track its progress, or mark it completed. Acknowledging an alert also does not necessarily mean the underlying work is finished.

## Proposed solution

Add persistent user tasks with a lifecycle independent of alert evaluation.

Each task should have:

- A stable ID.
- Title and description.
- Owner.
- Status: open, in progress, waiting, or completed.
- Optional due date.
- Creation, modification, and completion timestamps.
- A reference to the originating conversation or message.

When a user explicitly requests a task, save it immediately and confirm creation only after storage succeeds. Alert evaluation may enrich or escalate the task, but should not determine whether it exists.

Allow users to view, update, complete, and reopen tasks through the UI and chat. Provide authenticated API endpoints for the same operations, with pagination, filtering, ownership checks, and conflict detection.

Completed tasks should be hidden from active views by default but remain accessible in history.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use alerts as tasks:** Alert acknowledgement and dismissal do not accurately represent task progress or completion.
- **Use activity logs:** Logs record submissions but do not provide a reliable task lifecycle.
- **Require tasks to pass alert evaluation:** Explicit user commitments should persist regardless of their urgency or relevance score.

## Scope

- [x] Backend (`packages/core`)
- [x] UI (`packages/ui`)
- [ ] A new specialist agent
- [ ] An integration (Slack / Email / Telegram / Discord / Google Chat)
- [ ] Deployment / infrastructure
- [x] Docs

## Additional context

Tasks and alerts should have distinct purposes:

- **Task:** Work someone has committed to doing.
- **Alert:** Information selected for someone’s attention.

They may be linked, but acknowledging or dismissing an alert should not automatically complete its associated task.

### Acceptance criteria

- Explicitly requested tasks persist independently of alert evaluation.
- Creation is confirmed only after successful storage.
- Users can update status, complete tasks, and reopen them.
- UI, chat, and API reflect the same saved task state.
- Completed tasks are excluded from active views by default.
- Repeated requests or retries do not create unintended duplicates.
- Failed operations report an error without claiming success.

issues.title: Issues with scrollbar use in `Page` template main area
issues.body:
#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
In classic templates (Vanilla, Bootstrap, Fast, Material...), the scroll bar allowing to navigate within the main area was all the way to the right of the window which meant the cursor could be anywhere in the main area and it worked, even outside the actual main area container.

With `pn.ui.Page`, the scroll bar is within the main area container itself, with no margin, which proves frustrating to users.

First because on the web, to scroll through the main content of a page, you don't usually have to worry much about the position of your cursor. Plus, here it can become really bad if the main area is filled with elements that themselves can capture scroll events, such as plots, then the actual area where the scroll will reliably work can become vanishingly small. It's essentially only two tiny vertical bands on both sides of the plots.

Second, if you're looking for the scroll bar to actuate it by clicking on it, it's natural to look for it at the edge of the window.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
The idea would be to make `pn.ui.Page` behave like classic templates in that regard.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
I think one could set a larger main area width and then place the actual content between two spacers. But still you may not necessarily end up with the scroll bar at the edge of the window.

Attached is an example showing how hard it becomes to scroll within a main area filled with holoviews plots. Unfortunately the cursor is not visible but you get the idea.

```python
import holoviews as hv
import numpy as np
import panel as pn

pn.extension()

plots = pn.ui.Column(
    *[
        hv.Curve(np.random.randn(100)).opts(height=400, responsive="width")
        for _ in range(5)
    ],
    width=800,
)

page1 = pn.ui.Page(
    main=[plots],
    sidebar_width=250,
    sidebar=["## I'm the sidebar"],
    main_width=800,
    title="I'm a title",
)
page2 = pn.template.MaterialTemplate(
    main=[plots],
    sidebar_width=250,
    sidebar=["## I'm the sidebar"],
    title="I'm a title",
)

page1.servable()
# page2.servable()  # For comparison purposes
```

Flow scheduler stops firing jobs after some hours (eventlet worker); next_run_time stays in the past
issues.body:
Scheduled flows stop running without any error. The jobs stay in the jobstore, but their `next_run_time` stays in the past and nothing executes. Saving or re-activating a flow logs "Added job flow_workflow_N" with the new trigger time, but the job still doesn't fire. Manual runs keep working the whole time.

**Evidence** (checked on 2026-10-30 at about 09:02 IST)
Reading the jobstore table (`FLOW_JOBSTORE_TABLE`):

```
flow_workflow_23 2026-10-29 11:35:10   # interval flow, stuck since yesterday
flow_workflow_24 2026-10-29 11:36:02
flow_workflow_25 2026-10-29 11:36:02
flow_workflow_1  2026-10-30 08:55:00   # daily trigger, didn't fire at 08:55
```

At 08:54 the logs show `Creating daily trigger: 08:55` and `Added job flow_workflow_1`, but there's no log line at all at 08:55:00.

After `docker restart openalgo-web`, every job got a new future `next_run_time` and started firing again.

**Environment**

- Docker on ARM64 (Ubuntu).
- `gunicorn --worker-class eventlet --workers 1`.
- Container TZ, `tzlocal`, and the scheduler timezone are all `Asia/Kolkata`, so timezone isn't the cause.
- `BackgroundScheduler` with `SQLAlchemyJobStore` and `misfire_grace_time=60` (`services/flow_scheduler_service.py`).

**Suspected cause**
`BackgroundScheduler` runs in a thread under eventlet's monkey patching. The scheduler's wake-up thread seems to stall, so jobs are added but never woken. Possible fixes:

- Use `GeventScheduler` or an eventlet-friendly scheduler.
- Run the scheduler in a separate process.
- Add a watchdog that restarts the scheduler when a job's `next_run_time` falls behind.

Also, `misfire_grace_time=60` means a job that stalled is skipped instead of caught up. A missed scheduled run should at least be logged.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Activate flows with interval and daily schedule triggers.
2. Leave the container running for several hours. In my case it stalled about 1 hour after re-importing the flows on the previous day.
3. Check the jobstore `next_run_time` values. They're in the past and nothing runs until the container restarts.

issues.title: Remote Crew: let an edition provisioner put lifecycle controls on its crews' rows
issues.body:
### Existing issues

- [x] I searched open issues and this is not already requested.

### Problem

An edition can add a remote-provisioner lane: `registerRemoteProvisionerRenderer` draws its launch form. But once a crew is launched, its row in **Your crews** has no lifecycle controls. Stop / Start / Delete in the row menu exist only for EC2 crews, addressed by the launch tag.

So an edition that needs Start / Stop for its own machines must draw a second list of the same crews. Every crew then shows up twice, and only one copy has the buttons.

### Proposed behaviour

A frontend seam, `registerCrewRowActions`, keyed by the row's `provisioner_id` stamp. A contribution supplies up to two components, each handed the row:

- `menuItems`: extra items in the row's overflow menu, between Edit and Remove.
- `detail`: a block under the row header (the machine's state, an action in progress, its error).

Rules: the core registers nothing; `aws_ec2` cannot be claimed; a chained row (whose stamp the announcing pane chose) gets nothing; each component sits in an ErrorBoundary. Actions still go through the edition's own routes, which authorize server-side.

### Alternatives considered

Keep the edition's second list. It duplicates every crew and splits one crew's controls across two places.

### Anything else

Remote Crew (Settings → Remote Crew → Your crews)
