issues.title: [bug] Pinned-runner exemption skips the package review when npm's config adds a package to npx
issues.body:
## What happens

Since #6906, protect builds no package request for a pinned runner (`npx tsx …`, `npx vitest …` and the rest of the routine set) when the project's manifest, its installed copy and its lockfiles agree. The reasoning is that `npx` runs the local copy and fetches nothing.

That isn't always true for `npx`. `npm exec` reads the packages to install from npm's `package` setting (`const packages = this.npm.config.get('package')` in `lib/commands/exec.js`), and npm loads settings from the environment (`npm_config_package`, prefix matched without regard to case) and from every `.npmrc` it reads, including the project's own. When that setting names a package, libnpmexec skips the local `node_modules/.bin` lookup (`needPackageCommandSwap` is false), installs what the setting names, and runs the command with that package's bins first on `PATH`.

The verdict only reads the command's arguments, so for that launch protect builds no request, even though npm does fetch and run a package nobody reviewed.

Details: https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/pull/6906#issuecomment-6560965809

## Where

- Shipped in alpha builds since #6906 merged (`9f14e9caf7`). Confirmed in `alpha/v3.59.0a38`.
- Also in the 3.59.0 release PR (#6275). Stable 3.58.x doesn't have it.
- `bunx`: not checked. I don't know whether Bun has an equivalent setting.

## Expected

Protect keeps the package request for `npx` whenever npm's configuration names a package to install, and the exemption stays for ordinary settings such as `registry=`.

cc @kantorcodes @zerocodefast

issues.title: Proposal: optional SQLAlchemy storage adapter example for extension-owned data
issues.body:
## Proposal

Would a standalone, optional SQLAlchemy storage-adapter example for extension-owned relational data fit the extension-first direction?

Extensions that maintain auxiliary tables may need MySQL rather than SQLite, while core DeerFlow persistence and LangGraph checkpoints already have their own SQLite/PostgreSQL contracts. This proposal keeps those concerns separate and does not add a core MySQL backend.

## Scope

- Explicit backend/URL configuration; no environment-variable convention and no silent fallback.
- Provider-owned URL validation, engine creation and upsert syntax for SQLite/MySQL.
- Lazy sessions, application-owned schema initialization, explicit commit/rollback and terminal disposal.
- Validated connection-pool/socket budgets; SQLite foreign keys, WAL and bounded lock waits.
- Independent installation and SQLite/disposable-MySQL tests under an example directory, without changing default backend dependencies.

The implementation was extracted from an application use case, and its generic package has passed 32 independent tests against SQLite and disposable MySQL 8.4, including pool exhaustion, read timeouts and invalid idle connections. I would like feedback on whether this belongs as an example here or is better maintained externally. A draft PR will make the concrete scope reviewable.

## Boundaries

No business models, deployment configuration, data migrations, authentication changes, async framework persistence or checkpoint integration are proposed. Socket timeouts are not transaction-outcome guarantees, and writes are never automatically replayed.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, tests, extraction and this proposal. The accompanying PR will remain a draft with the human-review confirmation unchecked until the author completes that review.

issues.title: rewire router on chat reconnect when a room is cleaned up and recreated
issues.body:
Title: fix: rewire router on chat reconnect when a room is cleaned up and recreated

Body:


## Problem

`connect_chat` treats "chat_id already in `active_chats`" as a no-op:

    if chat_id in self.active_chats:
        self.log.warning(f"Chat {chat_id} already connected to router")
        return

When a collaboration room is torn down and recreated — e.g. the client's
WebSocket drops (browser tab closed, laptop sleeps) and the room is freed
after the document cleanup delay, then the user reopens the chat — the router
is *not* told the room went away (there is no stop/reset event when
`jupyter-server-documents` is not installed), so `active_chats[chat_id]` still
holds the old, stopped chat.

On reconnect, `connect_chat(chat_id, new_chat)` hits the stale guard and
returns early. Two consequences:

1. `message_observers[chat_id]` stays bound to the *old* chat's message stream,
   so messages typed in the recreated room are never routed (submitting a
   message does nothing).
2. `_notify_chat_init_observers` never fires, so the persona manager is never
   re-created and the bottom persona picker does not appear.

## Fix

Detect the reconnect case — same `chat_id` but a *different* chat object — and
rewire instead of bailing out: detach the old chat and notify stop observers,
then fall through to the normal connect path with the new chat.

    if chat_id in self.active_chats:
        if self.active_chats[chat_id] is chat:
            self.log.warning(f"Chat {chat_id} already connected to router")
            return
        self.log.warning(f"Chat {chat_id} reconnected with a new chat; rewiring router")
        self.disconnect_chat(chat_id)
        self._notify_chat_stop_observers(chat_id)

    self.active_chats[chat_id] = chat
Suggested commit message:


fix: rewire router when a chat reconnects after room cleanup

connect_chat bailed out whenever chat_id was already in active_chats.
After a room is freed and recreated (client disconnect + cleanup delay,
no stop event without jupyter-server-documents), the stale entry made
the router skip rewiring: new messages went unrouted and no persona
manager was recreated. Detect same-id/different-object and rewire.

issues.title: fix: stop the exact persona manager instance on chat stop (avoid killing a recreated manager)
issues.body:
## Problem

`_on_router_chat_stop` schedules the shutdown by ID only:

    task = self.event_loop.create_task(self._stop_persona_manager(chat_id))

and `_stop_persona_manager` re-fetches the manager by ID when the async task
finally runs:

    persona_manager = persona_managers.get(chat_id)
    ...
    finally:
        persona_managers.pop(chat_id, None)

If the chat reconnects in the meantime, `_on_router_chat_init` installs a fresh
`PersonaManager` for the same `chat_id` *before* the queued stop task runs. The
stop task then looks up by ID, shuts down the *new* manager, and unconditionally
pops the entry — tearing down the manager that just reconnected (persona picker
gone, messages unrouted).

## Fix

Capture the instance to stop synchronously in `_on_router_chat_stop` and pass it
through; `_stop_persona_manager` shuts down the captured instance and only
removes the settings entry if it still points at that same instance.

    def _on_router_chat_stop(self, chat_id: str) -> None:
        ...
        persona_manager = persona_managers.get(chat_id)
        if persona_manager is None:
            return
        task = self.event_loop.create_task(
            self._stop_persona_manager(chat_id, persona_manager)
        )
        self._stopping_chats[chat_id] = task

    async def _stop_persona_manager(
        self, chat_id: str, persona_manager: PersonaManager | None = None
    ) -> None:
        async with self._stop_lock:
            persona_managers = self.serverapp.web_app.settings['jupyter-ai']['persona-managers']
            if persona_manager is None:
                persona_manager = persona_managers.get(chat_id)
            if persona_manager is None:
                return
            try:
                await persona_manager.shutdown_personas()
                ...
            finally:
                if persona_managers.get(chat_id) is persona_manager:
                    persona_managers.pop(chat_id, None)
                self._stopping_chats.pop(chat_id, None)
Suggested commit message:


fix: stop the captured persona manager instance on chat stop

_on_router_chat_stop scheduled _stop_persona_manager(chat_id), which
re-fetched by ID when the async task ran; a reconnect installing a new
manager in between got shut down and popped instead. Capture the instance
up front and only pop the settings entry if it still matches.

issues.body:
## 📝 Background

ttnn.softmax_in_place and ttnn.scale_mask_softmax_in_place can silently return incorrect results for height-sharded inputs when used with SoftmaxShardedMultiCoreProgramConfig and the shard grid does not begin at core (0, 0). On affected offset grids, some shards are softmaxed while others are left unchanged with their input logits. The same failure pattern is reproducible on Wormhole and Blackhole in ttsim.

This is a correctness issue: the operation returns without an error, but the output can be substantially wrong. Sharded layer_norm and rms_norm on comparable offset grids are correct.
## 🎯 What Success Looks Like

    Fix both softmax_in_place and scale_mask_softmax_in_place for supported height-sharded inputs whose shard grid is offset from (0, 0).

    Fix both softmax_in_place and scale_mask_softmax_in_place for supported height-sharded inputs whose shard grid is offset from (0, 0).
    Add regression coverage for height-sharded inputs on grids at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 1), covering both ROW_MAJOR and COL_MAJOR orientations, with and without a mask.

    Add regression coverage for height-sharded inputs on grids at (0, 0), (1, 0), and (0, 1), covering both ROW_MAJOR and COL_MAJOR orientations, with and without a mask.
    Compare the output shard by shard against the corresponding PyTorch softmax result (including the masked result for scale_mask_softmax_in_place) using the repository's established correctness tolerances. Verify that every shard is updated and correct, not merely that the operation returns successfully.

    Compare the output shard by shard against the corresponding PyTorch softmax result (including the masked result for scale_mask_softmax_in_place) using the repository's established correctness tolerances. Verify that every shard is updated and correct, not merely that the operation returns successfully.
    Preserve correct behavior for origin-based shard grids and the existing supported configurations.

## 💡 Problem to Solve

The shared validate_sharded_input validation accepts an offset shard grid after comparing its bounding-box dimensions against compute_with_storage_grid_size. The sharded softmax factory, however, currently constructs its work range from (0, 0) and enumerates per-core runtime arguments from the origin. issues.title: [BUG] metric classes do not normalize array-like multioutput weights, results differ from the function versions
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

For forecasting error metric classes, an array-like `multioutput` is documented as averaging weights ("errors are averaged across variables, with values used as averaging weights"). `BaseForecastingErrorMetric._handle_multioutput` returns `df.dot(multioutput)` without dividing by the sum of the weights. The result is only correct when the weights sum to 1. With weights `[3, 7]`, `MeanAbsoluteError` and `MeanSquaredError` return values 10 times larger than the function versions `mean_absolute_error` and `mean_squared_error`, which use a weighted average.

**To Reproduce**

```python
import warnings

import numpy as np

from sktime.performance_metrics.forecasting import (
    MeanAbsoluteError,
    MeanSquaredError,
    mean_absolute_error,
    mean_squared_error,
)

warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

y_true = np.array([[0.5, 1], [-1, 1], [7, -6]])
y_pred = np.array([[0, 2], [-1, 2], [8, -5]])

w = [3, 7]
raw = MeanAbsoluteError(multioutput="raw_values")(y_true, y_pred)
print("raw MAE:", raw, "weighted average:", np.average(raw, weights=w))
print("function MAE:", mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred, multioutput=w))
print("class    MAE:", MeanAbsoluteError(multioutput=w)(y_true, y_pred))
print("function MSE:", mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred, multioutput=w))
print("class    MSE:", MeanSquaredError(multioutput=w)(y_true, y_pred))
```

Output:

```
raw MAE: [0.5 1. ] weighted average: 0.85
function MAE: 0.85
class    MAE: 8.5
function MSE: 0.825
class    MSE: 8.25
```

**Expected behavior**

The class returns the weighted average of the per-output errors, the same as the function: MAE 0.85 and MSE 0.825 for weights `[3, 7]`. Scaling all weights by a constant should not change the result.

**Additional context**

Root cause: `_handle_multioutput` uses a dot product for array-like `multioutput`:
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/b2ff96e496b676f81ccfe117f7e9f198d231fca0/sktime/performance_metrics/forecasting/_base.py#L842-L868

Documented meaning of array-like `multioutput` (averaging weights):
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/b2ff96e496b676f81ccfe117f7e9f198d231fca0/sktime/performance_metrics/forecasting/_base.py#L67-L75

The class docstring example uses `[0.3, 0.7]`, which already sums to 1, and the class skips its doctest, so this is not caught:
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/b2ff96e496b676f81ccfe117f7e9f198d231fca0/sktime/performance_metrics/forecasting/_mae.py#L99-L106

Possible fix: in `_handle_multioutput`, normalize array-like weights before the dot product, `w = np.asarray(multioutput, dtype=float); return df.dot(w / w.sum())`. With this change patched in locally, the reproducer gives class MAE 0.85 and class MSE 0.825, equal to the functions.

Related: #8635 (sample_weight rework of forecasting metrics), #9473 and #7304 (sample_weight PRs). The same missing normalization also exists for `sample_weight` in `_get_weighted_df` (time weights rather than output weights); I can file that separately or add it here, whichever is preferred.

issues.title: [BUG] metric classes do not normalize sample_weight, results scale with the weights and differ from the function versions
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`BaseForecastingErrorMetric._get_weighted_df` multiplies each time point's error by `sample_weight`, and the metric then takes a plain mean over time points. The result is `sum(w * e) / n` instead of the weighted average `sum(w * e) / sum(w)`. Multiplying all weights by a constant changes the result: with `sample_weight = 2 * ones`, `MeanAbsoluteError` returns 1.1 instead of the unweighted 0.55. The function versions `mean_absolute_error` and `mean_squared_error` (via `horizon_weight`) return the weighted average, so the class and function disagree for any weights whose mean is not 1.

**To Reproduce**

```python
import warnings

import numpy as np

from sktime.performance_metrics.forecasting import (
    MeanAbsoluteError,
    MeanSquaredError,
    mean_absolute_error,
    mean_squared_error,
)

warnings.simplefilter("ignore")

y_true = np.array([3, -0.5, 2, 7, 2])
y_pred = np.array([2.5, 0.0, 2, 8, 1.25])

print("unweighted class MAE:", MeanAbsoluteError()(y_true, y_pred))
for w in (np.full(5, 2.0), np.array([1.0, 1, 1, 1, 4])):
    print("weights", w)
    print("  function MAE:", mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred, horizon_weight=w))
    print("  class    MAE:", MeanAbsoluteError()(y_true, y_pred, sample_weight=w))
    print("  function MSE:", mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred, horizon_weight=w))
    print("  class    MSE:", MeanSquaredError()(y_true, y_pred, sample_weight=w))
```

Output:

```
unweighted class MAE: 0.55
weights [2. 2. 2. 2. 2.]
  function MAE: 0.55
  class    MAE: 1.1
  function MSE: 0.4125
  class    MSE: 0.825
weights [1. 1. 1. 1. 4.]
  function MAE: 0.625
  class    MAE: 1.0
  function MSE: 0.46875
  class    MSE: 0.75
```

**Expected behavior**

The class returns the weighted average over time points, equal to the function: MAE 0.55 and MSE 0.4125 for `2 * ones` (same as unweighted), MAE 0.625 and MSE 0.46875 for `[1, 1, 1, 1, 4]`.

**Additional context**

Root cause: the weights are multiplied in without normalization:
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/b2ff96e496b676f81ccfe117f7e9f198d231fca0/sktime/performance_metrics/forecasting/_base.py#L820-L840

and the result is then averaged with a plain mean, for example the default `_evaluate`:
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/b2ff96e496b676f81ccfe117f7e9f198d231fca0/sktime/performance_metrics/forecasting/_base.py#L387-L389
and `MeanSquaredError._evaluate`:
https://github.com/sktime/sktime/blob/b2ff96e496b676f81ccfe117f7e9f198d231fca0/sktime/performance_metrics/forecasting/_mse.py#L176-L178

Possible fix: in `_get_weighted_df`, multiply by `sample_weight / sample_weight.mean()`. Then the plain mean that follows equals `sum(w * e) / sum(w)`, and the `evaluate_by_index` values still average to `evaluate`. With this change patched in locally, the reproducer gives the function values for both weight vectors, for MAE and MSE.

Related: #8635 (sample_weight rework of forecasting metrics), #9473 and #7304 (sample_weight PRs, which do not change the normalization). The sibling problem for array-like `multioutput` weights (`_handle_multioutput`, dot product without normalization) is #11710; one fix could cover both.

issues.title: [Bug] Cancelling a Team run before member registration still starts delegated member runs
issues.body: ### Description Cancelling a background Team run during the manager's preflight can return successfully while the manager continues and starts new member runs afterward. In this reproduction, the cancel path sees no registered member run IDs, but the Team still delegates to its members. The parent eventually ends as `CANCELLED`, while both member runs end as `COMPLETED` and their tools execute. This is reproducible with Agno's real Team and AgentOS run/cancel routes. A deterministic local model is used only to control timing; no model API, ERP, or inventory service is called. ### Steps to Reproduce The reproduction bundle includes `run_team_cancel_repro.py` and `serve_team_cancel_demo.py`. 1. Install dependencies in the reproduction directory: ```powershell py -3.13 -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt ``` 2. Start the AgentOS demo server in terminal A. It does not automatically create or cancel a run: ```powershell $env:AGNO_MANUAL_PREP_DELAY_SECONDS = '8' $env:AGNO_MEMBER_TOOL_DELAY_SECONDS = '3' .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe .\serve_team_cancel_demo.py ``` 3. In terminal B, create a background run through the Team route: ```powershell $base = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000' $team = 'purchase-fulfillment-team' $session = 'manual-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N') $run = curl.exe -s -X POST "$base/teams/$team/runs" ` -F 'message=Review the local demo purchase order, check policy and reserve inventory.' ` -F "session_id=$session" ` -F 'user_id=manual-reviewer' ` -F 'stream=false' -F 'background=true' -F 'monitor=false' | ConvertFrom-Json $run | Format-List $runId = $run.run_id ``` 4. During the manager preflight delay, cancel the run through the Team route: ```powershell curl.exe -i -X POST "$base/teams/$team/runs/$runId/cancel?session_id=$session" ``` 5. Inspect parent/child state and local events after the member tools have had time to run: ```powershell Start-Sleep -Seconds 12 Invoke-RestMethod "$base/_demo/state/$runId`?session_id=$session" | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 12 ``` Alternatively, run three deterministic cases automatically: ```powershell .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe .\run_team_cancel_repro.py ``` ### Agent Configuration (if applicable) The harness creates a Team in `TeamMode.broadcast` with a manager and two members: - Inventory member calls a local `reserve_inventory` tool. - Compliance member calls a local `verify_purchase_policy` tool. - The local model adapter deterministically asks the manager to load the order and delegate to both members. - AgentOS serves the Team run and cancel routes. Tools write only to a local JSONL ledger. ### Expected Behavior If cancellation is requested during preflight, before the manager delegates to any members, the Team should observe the cancellation before starting new member runs. The parent should not report a cancelled run while newly delegated member runs continue to execute their tools and complete. ### Actual Behavior On Agno 3.1.12, all three automatic cases reproduced this sequence: - The cancel endpoint returned HTTP 200. - The cancellation path enumerated an empty member run ID list. - The manager continued after the cancellation response and requested Team delegation. - The compliance and inventory member tools wrote to the local ledger after the cancellation response. - The parent run ended as `CANCELLED`; both child runs ended as `COMPLETED`. ### Screenshots or Logs (if applicable) [team_cancel_issue_repro_bundle.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34400425/team_cancel_issue_repro_bundle.zip) ### Environment ```markdown - OS: Windows (10.0.26200) - Agno Version: `agno[os]==3.1.12` - Python: 3.13.13 - External Dependency Versions: `httpx==0.28.1`, `uvicorn==0.54.0` - Model: deterministic local adapter; no external model credentials - Additional Environment Details: AgentOS app served locally by Uvicorn on `127.0.0.1:8000`; mock tools do not connect to external business systems ``` ### Possible Solutions (optional) Check the Team cancellation state before processing manager tool calls that can start new member runs, and add a regression test for cancellation during preflight before any member run IDs have been registered. The intended behavior should be confirmed against the cancel API contract. ### Additional Context The Team cancel route describes cancellation as an attempt to stop execution gracefully and notes that it may not be immediate. This report focuses on new member runs starting after cancellation was requested and the final parent/child status disagreement; it does not assume already-running external operations can always be interrupted.

issues.title: [Bug] Condition and Loop dispatch later children after workflow cancellation
issues.body:
## Description

`Condition` and `Loop` can dispatch a later child after an earlier child has cancelled the workflow. The workflow eventually reports cancellation, but the later executor has already run and can perform unwanted side effects.

Affected paths observed locally:

| Container | Sync | Async | Sync streaming | Async streaming |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Condition` | later child runs | later child runs | stops correctly | stops correctly |
| `Loop` | later child runs | later child runs | later child runs | later child runs |

## Steps to Reproduce

Install a checkout with `python -m pip install -e libs/agno`. This public-API reproducer uses only function steps; no agent/model, database or service is required. The `effects` list records whether the later executor was invoked.

```python
import asyncio
from agno.run.base import RunContext
from agno.run.cancel import cancel_run
from agno.workflow import Condition, Loop, Step, Workflow
from agno.workflow.types import StepInput, StepOutput

for kind in ("Condition", "Loop"):
    for use_async in (False, True):
        for stream in (False, True):
            effects = []

            def cancel(step_input: StepInput, run_context: RunContext) -> StepOutput:
                effects.append("cancel")
                cancel_run(run_context.run_id)
                return StepOutput(content="cancelled")

            def write(step_input: StepInput) -> StepOutput:
                effects.append("write")
                return StepOutput(content="written")

            children = [Step(name="cancel", executor=cancel), Step(name="write", executor=write)]
            container = (
                Condition(evaluator=True, steps=children)
                if kind == "Condition"
                else Loop(max_iterations=2, steps=children)
            )
            workflow = Workflow(name="cancel-repro", steps=[container])

            async def run_async():
                if stream:
                    return [event async for event in workflow.arun(input="go", stream=True)]
                return await workflow.arun(input="go")

            if use_async:
                result = asyncio.run(run_async())
            else:
                result = workflow.run(input="go", stream=stream)
                if stream:
                    result = list(result)
            print(kind, use_async, stream, effects)
```

## Expected Behavior

Every case records only `['cancel']`. Once cancellation has been requested, the container should check it before dispatching another child. This does not require forcibly stopping an executor that is already running.

## Actual Behavior

Both non-streaming Condition cases and all four Loop cases record `['cancel', 'write']`. Streaming Conditions already record only `['cancel']`. In a non-streaming run, the final status is still `CANCELLED`, despite the later child having executed.

## Environment

- Source: current main `27479c63e0f94d9b3159894ad79cc768be4acf32` (also reproduced at `6e480286166086c23ab0d05dcec3a6530f0d5593`).
- Installed package metadata: Agno 3.1.12.
- Python 3.12.12; macOS 15.7.7.
- Local cancellation manager; no database-backed cancellation or live provider calls.

## Possible Solutions (optional)

Check cancellation before each child dispatch in the two non-streaming Condition methods and all four Loop methods, matching the checks already used by streaming Conditions. Checking only before each Loop iteration does not stop later children within that iteration.

## Additional Context

This is distinct from Parallel stream termination (#10390/#10391), Parallel cancellation status (#10882/#10908), and team-member dispatch (#11480/#11481). The reproducer contains no Parallel or Team and the problem is dispatching the next child after cancellation. Searches found no matching Condition/Loop fix.

This report was prepared with AI assistance and the reproduction was executed locally. The two containers are reported together because they violate the same child-dispatch cancellation boundary. No PR is being opened before maintainer triage.

issues.title: [Bug]: Runtime DSA metadata pin_memory failure (207001) terminates Prefill on A3 with v0.30.0rc2
issues.body:
### Your current environment

Manually collected package/build metadata and deployment settings are supplied instead of an unfiltered `collect_env.py` dump. No framework or allocator was invoked for this collection.

| Component | Observed version / configuration |
|---|---|
| Public image | `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.30.0rc2-a3` |
| vLLM package metadata | `0.30.0+empty` (not an exact source commit) |
| vLLM-Ascend | `0.30.0rc2` |
| PyTorch / TorchNPU | `2.10.0+cpu` / `2.10.0.post7` |
| TorchNPU embedded git version | `1d88b8608fd1e44545b5804026c7a57c44240bb4` |
| Hardware / host | A3, Linux aarch64, approximately 1 TiB host RAM |
| Driver recorded during investigation | `26.1.1`; exact CANN toolkit build is not included in this metadata collection |
| Prefill / Decode | Prefill DP4 x TP4; Decode DP8 x TP2; expert parallel enabled |
| Other installed native packages | `memfabric_hybrid==1.3.0`, `memcache_hybrid==1.3.0` |
| Workload | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 W8A8, DSA context parallel, DSpark, CPU Engram offload; Local cache configured for 384 GiB |

All host addresses, machine/container identifiers, filesystem deployment paths, business prompts, request identifiers and absolute incident timestamps are omitted. Framework-relative source paths and diagnostic error codes are retained.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Scope: runtime DSA metadata allocation is fatal to the Prefill engine.** This is not a report of startup Engram HostRegister failure, and it does not establish a memory leak or a unique CANN/driver defect.

A running Prefill worker failed in `vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/dsa_v41_cp.py:140`:

```python
common.seq_lens[: common.num_reqs] - suffix.pin_memory().to(
    common.seq_lens.device, non_blocking=True
)
```

The original Runtime/driver records at the same failure show a 64-byte Runtime Host request requiring an actual 2 MiB base-heap physical allocation. The driver allocation failed; TorchNPU raised `207001/EL0018`. The exception propagated through metadata construction and terminated the Prefill engine. The container subsequently exited with code 1 and `OOMKilled=false`.

#### Relevant configuration subset

This is a configuration excerpt, not a minimal deterministic reproducer. Networking and deployment identifiers are intentionally excluded.

```text
--data-parallel-size 4
--tensor-parallel-size 4
--enable-expert-parallel
--max-model-len 1048576
--max-num-batched-tokens 8192
--max-num-seqs 16
--block-size 128
--speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}'
--enforce-eager
--enable-prefix-caching
--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":true}'
--additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding":true,"enable_fused_mc2":1,"enable_dsa_cp":true,"enable_flashcomm1":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":true}'
```

An external shared Host KV cache was enabled. We have not established whether that configuration contributed to physical allocation pressure.

#### Reproduction status

The event occurred during ongoing inference, after model initialization had completed. We do not have a public prompt or a safe deterministic reproduction of the underlying physical allocation failure. We have not injected failures, changed allocator settings, or reproduced this on a newer release. The following is evidence of the observed failure, not a claim that the configuration above fails on every run.

#### Sanitized exception traceback

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1047, in _execute_worker_rpc
    output = func(*args, **kwargs)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py", line 375, in execute_model
    return self.worker.execute_model(scheduler_output)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py", line 791, in execute_model
    output = self.model_runner.execute_model(scheduler_output, intermediate_tensors)
             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "torch/utils/_contextlib.py", line 124, in decorate_context
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 2495, in execute_model
    (attn_metadata, spec_decode_common_attn_metadata) = self._build_attention_metadata(
                                                        ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 3876, in _build_attention_metadata
    _build_attn_group_metadata(
  File "vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 3799, in _build_attn_group_metadata
    attn_metadata_i = builder.build(
                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "vllm_ascend/attention/context_parallel/dsa_v41_cp.py", line 140, in build
    common.seq_lens[: common.num_reqs] - suffix.pin_memory().to(common.seq_lens.device, non_blocking=True)
                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch.OutOfMemoryError: allocate_host_memory_slowpath:../torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/CachingHostAllocator.cpp:252 NPU function error: aclrtMallocHostWithCfg, error code is 207001
[ERROR] <TIME> (PID=<PID>, <DEVICE_OR_RANK>, RankID:-1) ERR00100 PTA call acl api failed
[Error]: Failed to apply for memory.
        Check the remaining storage space in the hardware environment.
[PID=<PID>] <TIME>.323 Resource_Error_Insufficient_Host_Memory(EL0018): Failed to allocate 64 bytes host memory requested by the RUNTIME module.
        Possible Cause: Allocation failed due to insufficient host memory.
        Solution: Ensure that the required memory is available. Take measures such as stopping unnecessary processes to free memory.
TraceBack (most recent call last):
        Failed to allocate memory requested by RUNTIME module.
        rtsMallocHost execution failed, reason=driver error:out of memory[FUNC:FuncErrorReason][FILE:error_message_manage.cc][LINE:76]

```

#### Sanitized driver evidence

Only identifiers, addresses and time prefixes have been removed; allocation sizes, flags and error codes are preserved:

```text
devmm_virt_set_alloced_mem_struct:
  Can not alloc ptr. (ret_ptr=<STATUS>; alloc_ptr=<ADDR>;
  alloc_size=2097152; advise=117506565)
devmm_alloc_from_base_heap:
  Can not alloc physical memory from base heap.
  (ret_ptr=<STATUS>; va=<ADDR>; alloc_size=64; va=<ADDR>)
PeekLastErr: level=THREAD_LEVEL(0) err=207001
EL0018: Failed to allocate 64 bytes host memory requested by the RUNTIME module.
```

#### Component boundaries and code review

1. **vLLM-Ascend** owns the DSA metadata builder issuing the temporary `pin_memory()` request. The exception is not recovered at this point.
2. **TorchNPU** owns the Host caching allocator call. The installed wheel identifies git `1d88b860...`; the corresponding [CachingHostAllocator.cpp](https://github.com/Ascend/pytorch/blob/1d88b8608fd1e44545b5804026c7a57c44240bb4/torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/CachingHostAllocator.cpp) routes this call to `AclrtMallocHostWithCfg`. Its legacy-API fallback is for feature-not-supported; the observed `207001` is thrown. The installed ATen Host allocator header also makes a single slow-path allocation without an outer exception-based cache-reclaim retry.
3. **CANN/driver** is where the physical Host-UVA allocation failed. We do not have failure-time NUMA/buddy/watermark/quota or all pinned-page-owner data, so the cause of that failure remains unresolved. Total installed RAM and subsequent reboot success are not sufficient to diagnose a leak.

The wheel version metadata, ELF digest/RECORD and current worker loaded-library path were checked. That version correspondence is not a reproducible-build or instruction-by-instruction binary proof. We have not proved a reference driver source commit is byte-identical to the loaded driver.

#### Expected behavior / questions for maintainers

- What is the supported strategy for this runtime metadata path on this release: bounded preallocation/reuse, or a validated fallback that preserves metadata correctness?
- Can this failure be contained without terminating the entire engine? We are not suggesting continuing inference with incomplete metadata.
- Which targeted TorchNPU/CANN diagnostics would distinguish fragmentation/NUMA constraints, pinned-page ownership and driver resource limits for this Host-UVA path?
- Is there a maintained release/backport addressing this exact runtime metadata failure path? We will validate compatibility rather than assume an upgrade fixes the physical cause.

#### Related, not established duplicates

Related reports: #19485, #19934, #19721. Those concern startup Host registration/Engram scenarios; a shared error code does not establish the same root cause. This issue focuses on runtime DSA metadata `suffix.pin_memory()` and fatal exception propagation.

issues.title: [Feature] Native Persona Memories: Automatic Capture, Shared Profiles & Memory Manager
issues.body:
# Request Summary (Feature Overview & Motivation)

I'd like to propose a lightweight, native persistent memory system for Unsloth Studio, with automatic memory capture, flexible per-persona memory profiles, and a dedicated, user-editable Memory Manager.

The goal is to let personas remember important facts, preferences, experiences, relationships, character development, and decisions across conversations and different LLMs, without requiring external MCP servers, custom scripts, or manual memory-file maintenance.

**Persistent memory is especially important for roleplay and long-running character conversations.** Without it, personas repeatedly lose established relationships, shared experiences, important events, and their own character development whenever a new conversation begins.

This should be an optional feature, disabled by default, with full user control over stored memories.

## Table of Contents
(Sorry, I am NOT a Github professional so I needed to remove the entire anchor links, coz they didn't worked and jumped to everywhere!!!)

- Why AGENTS.md is not a practical replacement
- Proposed behavior
- 1 Optional memory functionality
- 2 Persistent memory profiles with flexible associations
- 3 Stable identity and backend-controlled ownership
- 4 Automatic memory capture
- 5 Roleplay and character continuity
- 6 Native memory operations
- 7 Dedicated Memories tab in the main navigation
- 8 Lightweight local storage — two possible approaches
- 9 System prompt integration
- 10 KV-cache and performance considerations
- 11 Memory quality and user control
- 12 Compatibility with PR #16729
- Suggested minimal implementation
- Related work
- Expected outcome

---

## Why AGENTS.md is not a practical replacement

The existing AGENTS.md implementation introduced in #13199 can be useful for persistent instructions and file-based notes.

However, **from a regular end-user's perspective, AGENTS.md is effectively not a usable conversational memory system.**

A normal chat user should not have to understand internal files, filesystem permissions, project agents, or tool execution simply to allow a persona to remember previous conversations.

In practice:

- AGENTS.md does not automatically identify and save meaningful conversational memories.
- Ordinary chat personas cannot necessarily edit or maintain the file themselves.
- Writing instructions in a system prompt does not grant missing file permissions or tools.
- There is no dedicated, user-friendly Memory Manager for reviewing and correcting stored information.
- Memory management depends on additional setup and mechanisms that ordinary users should not be expected to configure.
- It does not provide automatic per-persona memory separation or flexible profile sharing.

This is particularly limiting for roleplay users, where long-term continuity is a fundamental part of the experience rather than an optional convenience.

**AGENTS.md may remain useful for agent instructions and manually maintained notes, but it should not be considered a complete solution for persistent conversational memories.**

This proposal is intended to complement AGENTS.md, not replace it.

## Proposed behavior

### 1. Optional memory functionality

Add a native Memories feature with settings such as:

- Enable or disable persistent memories.
- Enable or disable automatic memory capture.
- Optionally require approval before saving suggested memories.
- Select the memory profile associated with a conversation.

When Memories are disabled, Unsloth should continue functioning normally without loading or creating memory entries.

### 2. Persistent memory profiles with flexible associations

**By default, every persona should receive its own dedicated memory profile.**

However, memory storage should not be permanently tied to a persona's display name, chat title, or underlying LLM.

Instead, each memory profile should have a stable internal ID managed by Unsloth.

Users should be able to choose between three options:

**A. Dedicated memory profile (default)**

Every persona has its own independent memories.

**B. Share an existing memory profile**

A newly created persona can use a memory profile already associated with another persona.

Both personas can access the same memories. Changes made by either persona are reflected in the shared profile.

Shared profiles should support:

- Read and write access (default).
- Optional read-only access.
- Clearly visible sharing status and permissions.
- Explicit user control over which personas can access the profile.

Read-only personas may retrieve memories but must not modify or delete them.

Permissions must be enforced by the backend, not merely through system prompt instructions.

**C. Copy memories from an existing profile**

A newly created persona can copy the memories of an existing persona.

The copied memories become independent, allowing the new persona to develop its own memories without modifying the original profile.

Ideally, copying could optionally support selecting individual entries.

These options should always be explicitly controlled by the user.

### 3. Stable identity and backend-controlled ownership

Memory profile associations must be enforced by Unsloth itself.

The model should never be responsible for generating, remembering, or selecting the authoritative memory profile ID.

Suggested behavior:

- Each memory profile receives an immutable internal identifier.
- Each conversation stores its assigned memory profile ID.
- Renaming a persona does not alter memory ownership.
- Changing the underlying LLM does not alter memory ownership.
- Users can explicitly reassign a conversation to another memory profile.
- Shared profiles are linked intentionally through the UI.
- Read/write permissions are enforced by Unsloth.
- Deleting a persona should not automatically destroy its memories without confirmation.

**The backend must determine which memory profile is active. The model must not be able to override that association or its permissions through generated text or tool arguments.**

### 4. Automatic memory capture

When automatic capture is enabled, Unsloth should allow the assistant to identify meaningful long-term information during ordinary conversations.

Potential examples:

- Persistent user preferences.
- Important experiences and decisions.
- Relevant personal information.
- Long-term conversational context.
- Persona-specific experiences and background information.
- Important agreements or previously established details.
- Significant roleplay events, relationships, and character development.

Temporary statements, guesses, duplicates, and unimportant conversational content should generally not be stored.

The application could process structured memory events from model output or use a lightweight extraction mechanism after completed responses.

The specific implementation can be left to the Unsloth developers.

The important requirements are:

- No external MCP server is needed.
- Users do not have to explicitly request every save operation.
- Memories are assigned to the correct profile by the backend.
- Failed memory operations are never reported as successful.
- Automatic capture should minimize additional inference overhead.

### 5. Roleplay and character continuity

**Persistent memory is a core requirement for meaningful long-term roleplay.**

A persona should be able to remember:

- Important shared experiences from previous conversations.
- Established relationships and their development.
- Significant events in an ongoing story.
- Character traits, preferences, and personal history.
- Previous decisions, commitments, and conflicts.
- Important details about the setting and narrative continuity.

For example, if two characters have established a relationship and experienced important events over several conversations, a new chat should not automatically erase that history.

The persona should be able to continue naturally, without requiring the user to repeatedly explain what happened before.

**Roleplay memories must remain associated with the appropriate persona or memory profile and should not automatically be interpreted as factual information about the real user.**

The system should allow fictional character memories and real-world user memories to remain separate when appropriate.

This distinction is particularly important because many users maintain different personas, settings, or fictional relationships.

A native memory system would substantially improve Unsloth Studio as a platform for long-running personal conversations and character-based interactions.

### 6. Native memory operations

The system should support:

- Add memories.
- Retrieve and search memories.
- Edit existing memories.
- Delete or mark outdated memories.
- Detect duplicates and possible contradictions.
- Optionally merge related memories.

User-made corrections should take precedence over automatically generated memory content.

Models should not silently recreate entries that the user deliberately deleted or corrected.

### 7. Dedicated Memories tab in the main navigation

**Please add a clearly visible, dedicated "Memories" tab to Unsloth Studio's main sidebar.**

It should not be hidden exclusively inside Settings, Projects, or an advanced developer interface.

Users need convenient access because LLMs sometimes save incorrect, duplicated, or misleading information.

The Memory Manager should allow users to:

- Select and switch between memory profiles.
- Create, rename, copy, and delete memory profiles.
- View which personas and conversations use a profile.
- Link an existing profile to another persona.
- Configure shared profiles as read/write or read-only.
- Disconnect a persona from a shared profile without deleting the underlying memories.
- Browse memory entries grouped by date or category.
- Expand and collapse groups.
- Add, edit, and delete individual memories.
- Change memory categories.
- Search memory contents.
- View source conversations where available.
- Review and correct AI-generated memories.
- Undo accidental changes where practical.
- Export and import memory profiles.

A simple list-based interface would be sufficient.

The existing persona/character management interface introduced through #16729 could additionally offer a "Memory profile" selector linking directly to this dedicated Memories tab.

### 8. Lightweight local storage — two possible approaches

Unsloth already uses SQLite for its internal persistence.

There are two reasonable implementation options.

**Option A: Separate memory database (preferred suggestion)**

Use a dedicated folder and SQLite database, for example:

`~/.unsloth/studio/memories/memories.db`

This is a proposed path, not an existing feature.

Benefits:

- Better separation from Unsloth's existing internal databases.
- Easier independent backup and restoration.
- Simpler export or migration of memories.
- Reduced coupling with the main Studio database schema.
- A storage pattern similar to Unsloth's existing separate RAG database.

**Option B: Additional tables in the existing Studio database**

Alternatively, Unsloth could integrate memory storage directly into its existing SQLite database.

Benefits:

- Reuse of existing persistence infrastructure.
- Fewer separate database files.
- Potentially simpler integration with chat and persona metadata.

Both approaches are acceptable. The developers should choose whichever fits the existing architecture and migration strategy best.

A minimal schema might include:

- `memory_id`
- `memory_profile_id`
- `category`
- `content`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`
- `source_thread_id` (optional)

An additional association table could link personas and conversations to memory profiles, including access permissions.

A simple SQLite-backed implementation should be sufficient for the first release.

No vector database, external database server, or knowledge graph should be required.

Storage should be included in Unsloth's backup/export system, with account-level separation where applicable.

### 9. System prompt integration

Users should not need to manually inject complete memory lists into custom system prompts.

Unsloth should internally provide the appropriate memory context based on the currently selected memory profile.

A stable, application-managed memory instruction could define how memories are used and when new memories should be proposed.

Custom system prompts may optionally influence what the persona considers relevant to remember.

However, they should not control memory profile ownership, database identifiers, or storage permissions.

**Memory functionality should work in ordinary chats, without requiring users to write special system prompt instructions or repeatedly command the model to remember something.**

If #16729 introduces a dedicated persona/character configuration, memory profile selection could be integrated there as well.

### 10. KV-cache and performance considerations

Preserving prompt caching is particularly important for local GGUF models and long conversations.

Please avoid rebuilding the beginning of the system prompt with an updated memory list after every response.

Possible approaches include:

- Loading an initial memory snapshot when a conversation starts.
- Retrieving additional relevant memories only when required.
- Appending contextual memory updates without rewriting the existing prompt prefix.
- Performing memory extraction after a completed response where practical.
- Avoiding an additional full-conversation inference pass for every message.

Memory capture and retrieval should not cause significant additional latency or repeated processing of large context windows.

It would be useful to keep memory extraction optional for users running smaller local models.

### 11. Memory quality and user control

LLMs can misunderstand statements, confuse roleplay with factual information, create duplicates, or store slightly inaccurate interpretations.

Therefore:

- Users must be able to inspect every stored memory.
- Every memory must remain editable and removable.
- Source references should be retained when practical.
- Fictional roleplay memories should remain distinguishable from factual user-profile memories.
- Deliberate user corrections should be respected.
- Automatic capture must not silently overwrite manually corrected memories.
- Shared profiles must be clearly identified.
- Read-only profiles must prevent model-generated modifications.
- Memory operations must be limited to the active, authorized profile.
- Separate users or accounts must not access each other's memories.

An optional approval mode could allow users to review proposed memories before saving them.

### 12. Compatibility with PR #16729

The ongoing work on characters, personas, group chats, and character card import in #16729 provides a promising integration opportunity.

Ideally, a persona could select its memory profile directly in the character settings.

However, the memory feature should not depend entirely on the completion of that PR.

Memory profiles should remain independently manageable and could also be assigned to ordinary chats without a dedicated character.

If character cards are imported, Unsloth should not silently associate them with existing memory profiles merely because their names match.

Users should explicitly decide whether imported personas receive new memories, copied memories, or access to an existing shared profile.

For group chats, each participating persona should retain its assigned memory profile unless the user deliberately configures shared memory.

## Suggested minimal implementation

A first release could remain relatively small:

1. Optional memory feature with an enable/disable setting.
2. SQLite-backed memory storage, either separate or integrated.
3. Stable memory profiles with backend-controlled associations.
4. One dedicated memory profile per persona by default.
5. Ability to link or copy an existing memory profile.
6. Basic read/write permissions for shared profiles.
7. Basic automatic memory capture and retrieval.
8. A visible Memories tab with viewing, editing, deletion, and profile selection.
9. Minimal impact on prompt caching and local inference performance.

Advanced semantic memory search, vector embeddings, complex knowledge graphs, and multi-agent orchestration could be considered later.

## Related work

- #10775 — Persistent Project and Agent Memory
- #12183 — Memory across conversations with different models
- #13199 — AGENTS.md support
- #16729 — Characters, personas, group chats, and character card import

This request is intentionally more specific than general persistent instructions or project-level notes.

The proposed feature focuses on automatic conversational memory, stable per-persona associations, optional profile sharing or copying, and complete user control through a dedicated interface.

## Expected outcome

A user creates a persona and enables Memories.

Unsloth automatically assigns a dedicated memory profile and allows the persona to remember meaningful information across conversations and different LLMs.

Later, the user creates another persona.

They can choose to:

- Start with completely new memories.
- Share the first persona's existing memory profile.
- Copy the first persona's memories and continue independently.

Shared memory profiles may optionally be configured as read-only for selected personas.

At any time, the user can open the dedicated Memories tab, inspect the stored information, correct inaccuracies, remove entries, and change profile assignments.

For long-running roleplay, the persona can retain established relationships, events, and character development across conversations without forcing the user to recreate the entire history.

**The result should be a lightweight, native, flexible memory system that respects user control, supports meaningful long-term character continuity, and remains practical for local inference. No external MCP server or additional memory service should be required.**

issues.title: ACI worker: start timeout is measured on the ARM LRO poller (30 s cadence) and deletes container groups that are already running
issues.body:
### Bug summary

### Bug summary

`AzureContainerWorker._wait_for_task_container_start` decides that a container failed to start by
watching only the ARM deployment `LROPoller` returned by `resource_client.deployments.begin_create_or_update`.
Two consequences, both observed in production on Azure Container Instances (eastus2) over Oct 25 to Nov 4, 2026,
on a pool creating ~500 container groups per day:

1. **The timeout fires against a 30-second poller.** `begin_create_or_update` is called without a polling
   interval, so the Azure SDK polls ARM every 30 s (visible in the Activity Log as `operationStatuses/read`
   every 30 s). The worker checks `creation_status_poller.done()` every `task_watch_poll_interval` (5 s)
   and raises at exactly `task_start_timeout_seconds`. Up to 30 s of the budget is lost to poller
   granularity. In 5 runs the ARM deployment had already reached `Succeeded` 1 to 19 seconds before the
   worker raised and deleted the group:

   | ARM deployment Succeeded | worker `containerGroups/delete` | margin |
   |---|---|---|
   | 12:04:37 | 12:04:56 | 19 s |
   | 14:24:40 | 14:24:53 | 13 s |
   | 22:10:37 | 22:10:40 | 3 s |
   | 04:06:46.9 | 04:06:48.3 | 1.4 s |
   | 00:34:47 (container group), 00:34:56 (deployment) | 00:34:55 | 7 s |

2. **A running container is killed.** On timeout, `run()`'s `finally` branch calls
   `_wait_for_container_group_deletion` without reading the container group's instance view or the flow
   run state. In 2 runs the container had been `Running` for 2 min and 3.5 min (flow run in `Running`,
   logs flowing, dbt executing) while the ARM operation stayed `Running` on Azure's side; the worker
   deleted the group and reported the flow run as
   `Crashed: Failed to submit flow run to infrastructure: RuntimeError: Timed out after 300.0s while watching waiting for container start.`
   Example timeline (UTC): `containerGroups/write` Started 02:36:40 → ACI event `Started container`
   02:37:53 → flow run Running 02:38:07 → ARM `operationStatuses` still `Running` at 02:41:12 →
   worker delete 02:41:40 → ARM write `Canceled` 02:41:49.

Because the flow run was already `Running`, the run is not retried by anything that keys on
`run_count == 0`, and the message blames submission although the infrastructure was up.

The root trigger is slow ACI provisioning (image pulls of 3.5 to 4 min), but the worker turns a
slow start into a lost run. Raising `task_start_timeout_seconds` only moves the race.

### Expected behavior

- The start wait should treat the container being up as "started": poll the container group's
  `instance_view` (or the flow run state) in the loop, and stop waiting once the container is `Running`,
  regardless of the ARM LRO.
- The poller's cadence should match the worker's: pass `polling_interval=configuration.task_watch_poll_interval`
  (or an explicit `ARMPolling`) to `begin_create_or_update`, or drop the LRO and poll the group directly.
- On timeout, do not delete a container group whose container is `Running`; hand it to
  `_watch_task_and_get_exit_code` instead (or at minimum make deletion conditional on the container not
  having started). This matches the Kubernetes worker, where `pod_watch_timeout_seconds` only covers the
  pod reaching `Running`.

### Reproduction

Hard to force on demand because it depends on ACI provisioning time. Deterministic variant: set
`task_start_timeout_seconds` to a value a few seconds below the typical provisioning time of the region
(for us ~90 s is normal, so set 85) and run a long flow; the worker deletes groups whose container has
already started and whose ARM deployment succeeds within the next poll interval.

Code (unchanged on `main` as of Nov 4, 2026, `src/integrations/prefect-azure/prefect_azure/workers/container_instance.py`):

```python
while not creation_status_poller.done():
    elapsed_time = time.time() - t0
    if timeout and elapsed_time > timeout:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Timed out after {elapsed_time}s while watching waiting for container start."
        )
    time.sleep(configuration.task_watch_poll_interval)

creation_status_poller = await run_sync_in_worker_thread(
    resource_client.deployments.begin_create_or_update,
    resource_group_name=configuration.resource_group_name,
    deployment_name=f"prefect-{container_group_name}",
    parameters=deployment,
)

### Version info

```Text
Worker runs in a self-built image (Prefect 3.8.4 OSS fork, Python 3.12, self-hosted server). Pinned by
the image's uv.lock:

- prefect 3.8.4 (fork of PrefectHQ/prefect 3.8.4; `prefect_azure` is the unmodified PyPI package)
- prefect-azure 0.4.11 — `prefect_azure/workers/container_instance.py` is identical in 0.4.11, 0.4.13 and current `main`
- azure-core 1.38.0
- azure-mgmt-resource 24.0.0
- azure-mgmt-containerinstance 10.1.0
- azure-mgmt-core 1.6.0
- azure-identity 1.25.1
- httpx 0.28.1, pydantic 2.13.4
```

### Additional context

Additional context

- Observed on 8 runs out of 222 start timeouts in 11 days; the other timeouts are genuine ACI placement
  failures (Failed to pull image ... CriContainerActivator is getting initialized and not ready for use)
  and are being raised with Microsoft separately.
- Evidence comes from the Azure Activity Log of the resource group (deployments/write,
  containerGroups/write, operationStatuses/read, containerGroups/delete with timestamps) and from
  ContainerEvent_CL in Log Analytics (Started container events).

issues.title: `HyperParameterTuningJob.create` rejects tuner tags on Python 3.14
issues.body:
**PySDK Version**
- [ ] PySDK V2 (2.x)
- [x] PySDK V3 (3.x)

**Describe the bug**

Tagged `HyperparameterTuner` requests fail validation on Python 3.14.
Equivalent requests succeed on Python 3.12.

The tuner creates request tags as `sagemaker.core.shapes.Tag`.
On Python 3.14, `HyperParameterTuningJob.create()` resolves its `tags`
annotation as `list[sagemaker.core.resources.Tag]`.

Both classes have the same `key` and `value` fields. However, they are separate
Pydantic models. Pydantic rejects the shapes model instead of converting it to
the generated resource model.

The failure occurs before the SDK calls SageMaker.

This is not a SageMaker v3.28 regression. The behavior also reproduces with the
v3.27 component set on Python 3.14.

**To reproduce**

Save this script as `reproduce.py`. It does not call a live AWS service.

```python
import importlib.metadata
import inspect
import sys

from pydantic import TypeAdapter
from sagemaker.core.resources import HyperParameterTuningJob
from sagemaker.core.shapes import Tag

tags_annotation = inspect.signature(
    HyperParameterTuningJob.create
).parameters["tags"].annotation

print("Python:", sys.version)
print("SageMaker:", importlib.metadata.version("sagemaker"))
print("SageMaker Core:", importlib.metadata.version("sagemaker-core"))
print("Resource annotation:", tags_annotation)

validated_tags = TypeAdapter(tags_annotation).validate_python(
    [
        Tag(
            key="project",
            value="hpo-tag-reproduction",
        )
    ]
)

print("Validated tags:", validated_tags)
```

Run it with Python 3.12:

```bash
uvx --python 3.12 --from sagemaker==3.28.0 python reproduce.py
```

The script succeeds. The annotation resolves to
`sagemaker.core.shapes.Tag`.

Run it with Python 3.14:

```bash
uvx --python 3.14 --from sagemaker==3.28.0 python reproduce.py
```

The script fails. The annotation resolves to
`sagemaker.core.resources.Tag`.

The same mismatch occurs during `HyperparameterTuner.tune()`. The tuner creates
its request tags with this code:

```python
from sagemaker.core.shapes import Tag

tag_objects = [
    Tag(key=boto_tag["Key"], value=boto_tag["Value"])
    for boto_tag in (_to_boto_tag(tag) for tag in self.tags)
]
```

**Expected behavior**

`HyperParameterTuningJob.create()` must accept the tag model produced by
`HyperparameterTuner` on every supported Python version.

**Screenshots or logs**

Python 3.14 produces this error:

```text
Resource annotation: typing.List[sagemaker.core.resources.Tag] | None
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError:
1 validation error for nullable[list[Tag]]
0
  Input should be a valid dictionary or instance of Tag
  [type=model_type,
   input_value=Tag(key='project', value='hpo-tag-reproduction'),
   input_type=Tag]
```

**System information**

- **SageMaker Python SDK version**: 3.28.0
- **SageMaker Core version**: 2.28.0
- **SageMaker Train version**: 1.28.0
- **Framework name (eg. PyTorch) or algorithm (eg. KMeans)**: Framework-independent
- **Framework version**: Not applicable
- **Python version**: 3.14
- **CPU or GPU**: CPU
- **Custom Docker image (Y/N)**: Reproduces before image selection

**Additional context**

Python 3.14 uses deferred annotation evaluation. The unqualified `Tag` name
resolves after `sagemaker.core.resources.Tag` exists in the module.

Earlier Python versions capture the imported `sagemaker.core.shapes.Tag` when
the function is defined.

A stable fix can import the public shape with an unambiguous alias:

```python
from sagemaker.core.shapes import Tag as ShapeTag

def create(
    # ...
    tags: list[ShapeTag] | None = None,
):
    ...
```

Tests must exercise tagged HPO request validation on Python 3.14.

issues.title: `HyperparameterTuner` uploads local source without the `ModelTrainer` KMS key
issues.body:
**PySDK Version**
- [ ] PySDK V2 (2.x)
- [x] PySDK V3 (3.x)

**Describe the bug**

`HyperparameterTuner` manually creates and uploads `sourcedir.tar.gz` when its
`ModelTrainer` uses a local `SourceCode.source_dir`.

The upload calls `s3_client.upload_file()` without `ExtraArgs`. It does not use
the KMS key from `ModelTrainer.output_data_config.kms_key_id`.

This differs from `ModelTrainer.create_input_data_channel()`. That method uses
the output KMS key for local source uploads when no explicit key is supplied.

The tuner also uploads directly to `session.default_bucket()`. This bypasses
the trainer's staging-bucket resolution.

The resulting object can use the wrong encryption key. The upload can also
fail when a bucket policy requires explicit SSE-KMS request headers.

Bucket default encryption can mask the problem. It does not make the configured
trainer KMS key effective.

**To reproduce**

Run this script. It does not call a live AWS service.

```python
import os
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import boto3
from sagemaker.core.helper.session_helper import Session
from sagemaker.core.training.configs import Compute, OutputDataConfig, SourceCode
from sagemaker.train import ModelTrainer
from sagemaker.train.tuner import HyperparameterTuner

role = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/example"
kms_key = (
    "arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:123456789012:"
    "key/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
)

with TemporaryDirectory() as source_dir:
    with open(
        os.path.join(source_dir, "train.py"),
        "w",
        encoding="utf-8",
    ) as script:
        script.write('print("test")\n')

    boto_session = boto3.Session(
        aws_access_key_id="test",
        aws_secret_access_key="test",
        region_name="us-east-2",
    )
    session = Session(boto_session=boto_session)
    session.default_bucket = lambda: "default-bucket"

    with patch(
        "sagemaker.train.defaults.resolve_and_validate_role",
        return_value=role,
    ):
        trainer = ModelTrainer(
            training_image=(
                "123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/"
                "example:latest"
            ),
            role=role,
            sagemaker_session=session,
            source_code=SourceCode(
                source_dir=source_dir,
                entry_script="train.py",
            ),
            compute=Compute(
                instance_type="ml.m5.large",
                instance_count=1,
                volume_size_in_gb=20,
            ),
            output_data_config=OutputDataConfig(
                s3_output_path="s3://output-bucket/jobs",
                kms_key_id=kms_key,
            ),
        )

    s3_client = MagicMock()

    with (
        patch.object(
            ModelTrainer,
            "create_input_data_channel",
            return_value=MagicMock(),
        ),
        patch.object(
            boto_session,
            "client",
            return_value=s3_client,
        ),
    ):
        HyperparameterTuner._build_driver_and_code_channels(trainer)

    upload_call = s3_client.upload_file.call_args
    expected_extra_args = {
        "ServerSideEncryption": "aws:kms",
        "SSEKMSKeyId": kms_key,
    }

    print("Upload bucket:", upload_call.args[1])
    print("Upload key:", upload_call.args[2])
    print("Upload keyword arguments:", upload_call.kwargs)
    print("Expected ExtraArgs:", expected_extra_args)

    assert upload_call.kwargs.get("ExtraArgs") == expected_extra_args
```

The assertion fails because the upload has no keyword arguments.

**Expected behavior**

The HPO source archive upload must use
`ModelTrainer.output_data_config.kms_key_id`.

The tuner should reuse `ModelTrainer.create_input_data_channel()` or its upload
helpers instead of implementing a separate S3 upload.

**Screenshots or logs**

```text
Upload bucket: default-bucket
Upload key: test-job/tuning-1234567890/input/sourcedir/sourcedir.tar.gz
Upload keyword arguments: {}
Expected ExtraArgs: {'ServerSideEncryption': 'aws:kms', 'SSEKMSKeyId': 'arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:123456789012:key/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'}
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
AssertionError
```

**System information**

- **SageMaker Python SDK version**: 3.28.0
- **SageMaker Core version**: 2.28.0
- **SageMaker Train version**: 1.28.0
- **Framework name (eg. PyTorch) or algorithm (eg. KMeans)**: Framework-independent
- **Framework version**: Not applicable
- **Python version**: 3.12
- **CPU or GPU**: CPU
- **Custom Docker image (Y/N)**: Reproduces with either

**Additional context**

The direct upload is:

```python
s3_client.upload_file(tar_path, bucket, s3_key)
```

`ModelTrainer._resolve_upload_extra_args()` already creates the required
`ExtraArgs` dictionary. Reusing that method would preserve current trainer
behavior.

A regression test must verify the bucket, key, and `ExtraArgs` values. It must
also cover an omitted KMS key.

issues.title: `ModelTrainer.train` discards the local artifact path and stores no local job state
issues.body:
**PySDK Version**
- [ ] PySDK V2 (2.x)
- [x] PySDK V3 (3.x)

**Describe the bug**

`ModelTrainer.train()` exposes remote training state through
`_latest_training_job`.

Local training behaves differently. `_LocalContainer.train()` returns the
local model artifact path, but `ModelTrainer.train()` discards that return
value. It also leaves `_latest_training_job` unset.

The generated local training job name is only written to a log message.
Callers cannot retrieve the local job name or model artifact path from the
trainer.

This prevents shared code from handling local and remote training results
consistently.

**To reproduce**

Run this script. It does not start Docker or call a live AWS service.

```python
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import boto3
from sagemaker.core.helper.session_helper import Session
from sagemaker.core.training.configs import Compute
from sagemaker.train import ModelTrainer
from sagemaker.train.model_trainer import Mode

role = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/example"

boto_session = boto3.Session(
    aws_access_key_id="test",
    aws_secret_access_key="test",
    region_name="us-east-2",
)
session = Session(boto_session=boto_session)

with patch(
    "sagemaker.train.defaults.resolve_and_validate_role",
    return_value=role,
):
    trainer = ModelTrainer(
        training_image="example:latest",
        training_mode=Mode.LOCAL_CONTAINER,
        role=role,
        sagemaker_session=session,
        compute=Compute(
            instance_type="local",
            instance_count=1,
            volume_size_in_gb=20,
        ),
    )

training_request = {
    "training_job_name": "local-test-job",
    "resource_config": trainer.compute,
    "algorithm_specification": MagicMock(
        training_image="example:latest",
        container_entrypoint=None,
        container_arguments=None,
    ),
    "input_data_config": [],
    "hyper_parameters": {},
    "environment": {},
}

local_container = MagicMock()
local_container.train.return_value = "file:///tmp/model.tar.gz"

with (
    patch.object(
        ModelTrainer,
        "_create_training_job_args",
        return_value=training_request,
    ),
    patch(
        "sagemaker.train.model_trainer._LocalContainer",
        return_value=local_container,
    ),
):
    result = trainer.train()

print("ModelTrainer result:", result)
print("Latest training job:", trainer._latest_training_job)
print("Local container result:", local_container.train.return_value)

assert result == "file:///tmp/model.tar.gz"
```

The assertion fails because `ModelTrainer.train()` returns `None`.

**Expected behavior**

After local training, callers must be able to retrieve:

- The generated local training job name.
- The local model artifact path.
- The local output artifact path, when available.

`ModelTrainer.train()` can return a local result object or store this state on
the trainer. The remote behavior must remain compatible.

**Screenshots or logs**

```text
ModelTrainer result: None
Latest training job: None
Local container result: file:///tmp/model.tar.gz
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
AssertionError
```

**System information**

- **SageMaker Python SDK version**: 3.28.0
- **SageMaker Core version**: 2.28.0
- **SageMaker Train version**: 1.28.0
- **Framework name (eg. PyTorch) or algorithm (eg. KMeans)**: Framework-independent
- **Framework version**: Not applicable
- **Python version**: 3.12
- **CPU or GPU**: CPU
- **Custom Docker image (Y/N)**: Reproduces before image execution

**Additional context**

The local branch currently calls:

```python
local_container.train(wait)
```

It can preserve the existing return value:

```python
local_artifact_path = local_container.train(wait)
```

The returned value identifies `model.tar.gz`. `_LocalContainer` also knows the
generated job name and creates `output.tar.gz`.

Regression tests must cover local result access and unchanged remote behavior.
